questions.passage: Ironically, years later, he seems to be happier with his decision than I. This may sound like the makings of a Chinese proverb, but it illustrates a larger truth: psychological research shows that trying to make others happy will make you happy, while trying to make yourself happy sometimes fails to do so. Indeed, psychologists have found that prosocial spending, writing gratitude letters, and having a satisficer (i.e., happy with good enough) mindset all promote happiness.
questions.prompt: Which paraphrase best matches the passage’s comparison of happiness-seeking strategies?
options: Self-focused efforts bring happiness more reliably than helping others.
Helping others brings happiness through the gratitude they return.
The approaches listed promote happiness through financial generosity.
Helping others can bring happiness; self-focused efforts may fail.
questions.promptZh: 哪一改写最符合本段对追求幸福方式的比较？
optionsZh: 专注自身的努力比帮助他人更可靠地带来幸福。
帮助他人通过对方回报的感激带来幸福。
所列方法都通过金钱上的慷慨促进幸福。
帮助他人可以带来幸福，而专注自身的努力有时会失败。
analyses: A 把原文对两种追求方式的对比倒置。原文强调努力使自己幸福有时并不奏效，没有说这种方式更可靠。
B 原文没有把对方回报的感激设为起作用的机制。writing gratitude letters 是写信表达自己的感激，不能换成收到他人的感激。
C 清单还包含写感恩信和满意即可的心态，不能把共同机制归结为花钱。
D 对应 make others happy will make you happy 与 make yourself happy sometimes fails；保留他人导向的益处和自我导向可能失败的区别。

evidence.quote: psychological research shows that trying to make others happy will make you happy, while trying to make yourself happy sometimes fails to do so.

vocabulary.meaning: 知足者；接受足够好结果的人
vocabulary.context: 作者用 happy with good enough 解释这种心态
vocabulary.example: A satisficer may choose a suitable option without comparing every alternative.
collocations: a satisficer rather than a maximizer

questions.translation: 具有讽刺意味的是，多年后，父亲似乎比我更满意自己的决定。这听起来像是中国谚语的素材，却说明了一个更普遍的道理：心理学研究显示，努力让别人幸福也会使自己幸福，而努力让自己幸福有时反而做不到。的确，心理学家发现，亲社会支出、写感恩信，以及知足者心态，也就是对足够好的结果感到满意，都能促进幸福。
questions.editorialStatus: 按第 1 章 PDF 第 9–16 页具体原文编写；保持已发布短段边界；区分叙事、研究概括、比喻与引文

questions.passage: A psychologically rich life is a life filled with diverse, unusual, interesting experiences that change your perspective; a life with twists and turns; a dramatic, eventful life instead of a simple and straightforward one; a life with multiplicity and complexity; a life with lots of stops, detours, and turning points; a life that feels like a long, winding hike rather than many laps of the same racing circuit.
questions.prompt: Which feature is central to the author’s definition of a psychologically rich life?
options: Varied experiences that change one's perspective.
Personal contentment maintained through familiar, predictable experiences.
Purposeful experiences guided by a stable central goal.
Repeated experiences that deepen expertise without changing viewpoints.
analyses: A diverse, unusual, interesting experiences that change your perspective 直接支持这一概括，后面的曲折、复杂和转折继续展开这个特征。
B 当前句强调不同寻常、多样和视角改变，并未以熟悉、可预测的满足感定义心理丰富。
C 句中没有把稳定的核心目标设为定义标准；这里的重点是经历的多样性和视角变化。
D without changing viewpoints 与 change your perspective 相反；反复进行同样的活动也与同一跑道绕圈这一对照意象更接近。

evidence.quote: A psychologically rich life is a life filled with diverse, unusual, interesting experiences that change your perspective;

vocabulary.context: 有些经历会改变看待世界的方式
vocabulary.example: Travel gave her a new perspective on work.

questions.editorialStatus: 短段版 v2；连续原句，配题片段互不重叠；保留 v1 历史快照，不重算旧成绩
questions.translation: 心理丰富的人生，充满多样、不同寻常、有趣且能改变视角的经历；它曲折多变，充满戏剧性与事件，而非简单平直；它有多重性与复杂性，有许多停顿、绕道与转折；它感觉像漫长蜿蜒的徒步，而不是在同一个跑道上反复绕圈。
questions.promptZh: 作者定义的心理丰富人生，其核心特征是什么？
optionsZh: 多样且能改变个人视角的经历。
通过熟悉、可预测的经历维持个人满足感。
由稳定的核心目标引导的有目的经历。
加深专长却不改变视角的重复经历。

questions.passage: Then, in 1989, Carol Ryff published a paper entitled “Happiness Is Everything, or Is It?,” presenting an alternative model of a good life that focused on autonomy, self-acceptance, purpose, positive relations, environmental mastery, and personal growth.
questions.prompt: Which combination belongs to Carol Ryff’s alternative model described here?
options: Autonomy, purpose, and personal growth.
Self-acceptance, social status, and personal growth.
Positive relations, obedience, and environmental mastery.
Physical comfort, purpose, and self-acceptance.
questions.promptZh: 哪组要素属于这里描述的 Carol Ryff 的替代模型？
optionsZh: 自主性、目标感和个人成长。
自我接纳、社会地位和个人成长。
积极关系、服从和环境掌控。
身体舒适、目标感和自我接纳。
analyses: A autonomy、purpose 和 personal growth 都出现在原文的六项要素中。
B 自我接纳与个人成长在清单中，但 social status 不在。不能因两项正确就接受整组。
C positive relations 与 environmental mastery 在清单中，但 obedience 不在；原文写的是 autonomy。
D purpose 和 self-acceptance 在清单中，physical comfort 不在。此题要求整组均属于模型。

evidence.quote: an alternative model of a good life that focused on autonomy, self-acceptance, purpose, positive relations, environmental mastery, and personal growth.

vocabulary.context: Ryff 模型列出的一个维度，并非免除全部责任
vocabulary.example: The course gives learners greater autonomy over their schedules.

questions.translation: 随后在 1989 年，Carol Ryff 发表了题为《Happiness Is Everything, or Is It?》的论文，提出一种关于美好生活的替代模型，关注自主性、自我接纳、目标感、积极关系、环境掌控和个人成长。
questions.editorialStatus: 按第 1 章 PDF 第 9–16 页具体原文编写；保持已发布短段边界；区分叙事、研究概括、比喻与引文

questions.passage: Along with Ed Deci and Richard Ryan’s self-determination theory, Ryff’s approach to the good life has come to be called the “eudaimonic approach”—a meaningful life, in short —in contrast to Ed Diener, Daniel Kahneman, Dan Gilbert, Sonja Lyubomirsky, and others’ approach to the good life, which has come to be called the “hedonic approach”—a happy life.
questions.prompt: How does the passage distinguish the eudaimonic and hedonic approaches?
options: Happiness in the former; meaning in the latter.
The former is linked to Diener; the latter to Ryff.
Meaning in the former; happiness in the latter.
The former concerns purpose; the latter rejects pleasure.
analyses: A 将两种取向的对应关系颠倒：原文把 eudaimonic 概括为 meaningful life，把 hedonic 概括为 happy life。
B 把人物归属颠倒。句中 Ryff 一侧对应 eudaimonic，Diener 等人一侧对应 hedonic。
C 两个破折号后的 a meaningful life 与 a happy life 直接支持前者意义、后者幸福的对应。
D 后半项 rejects pleasure 没有原文依据，不能从 happy life 推出排斥愉悦；一部分听似合理也不能使整项成立。

evidence.quote: the “eudaimonic approach”—a meaningful life, in short
the “hedonic approach”—a happy life.

vocabulary.context: 侧重有意义生活的研究取向
vocabulary.example: The eudaimonic approach considers purpose and development.

questions.editorialStatus: 短段版 v2；连续原句，配题片段互不重叠；保留 v1 历史快照，不重算旧成绩
questions.translation: 里夫关于美好生活的取向，与埃德·德西和理查德·瑞安的自我决定理论一起，被称为“实现论取向”——简言之，是有意义的生活。与之相对，埃德·迪纳、丹尼尔·卡尼曼、丹·吉尔伯特、索尼娅·柳博米尔斯基等人的取向被称为“享乐论取向”——幸福的生活。
questions.promptZh: 文中如何区分实现论取向与享乐论取向？
optionsZh: 前者关联幸福，后者关联意义。
前者关联迪纳，后者关联里夫。
前者关联意义，后者关联幸福。
前者关注目的，后者排斥愉悦。

questions.passage: How we think about our intelligence—specifically, whether we believe that intelligence can be improved—is also important in predicting intelligence and human performance, she showed.
questions.prompt: Which belief is singled out as relevant to predicting intelligence and performance?
options: People's performance depends on inherited intelligence alone.
How people view their intelligence makes little predictive difference.
Improving performance means accepting one's current intellectual limits.
Intelligence is something that can be improved.
questions.promptZh: 哪种观念被特别指出与预测智力和表现有关？
optionsZh: 人的表现只取决于遗传的智力。
人们如何看待自己的智力，对预测几乎没有影响。
提升表现意味着接受自己现有的智力上限。
智力是可以得到提高的。
analyses: A 当前句没有把表现归结为遗传这一唯一因素，反而强调人如何看待自己的智力也很重要。
B little predictive difference 与 also important in predicting 相反。
C 句子特别指出能否提高的信念，没有把接受固定上限作为提升表现的含义。
D whether we believe that intelligence can be improved 明确指出所谈的信念。题目问的是哪种观念被提及，不是仅凭本句证明任何人的智力都一定会提高。

evidence.quote: whether we believe that intelligence can be improved—is also important in predicting intelligence and human performance

vocabulary.context: 此处说观念对预测表现有重要性，不等于独自决定表现
vocabulary.example: Past practice can be useful in predicting future performance.

questions.translation: 她指出，我们如何看待自己的智力——具体说，是否相信智力可以提高——对于预测智力和人的表现也很重要。
questions.editorialStatus: 按第 1 章 PDF 第 9–16 页具体原文编写；保持已发布短段边界；区分叙事、研究概括、比喻与引文

questions.passage: My son’s suggestion motivated me to fix the window and become a better handyman, a small example of how concepts like growth mindsets broaden the way we think about the self, others, and the world.
questions.prompt: What effect did the son’s comment have on the author?
options: It persuaded him to leave repairs to experienced workers.
It encouraged him to attempt a practical repair.
It shifted his attention from repair skills to family relationships.
It convinced him that thinking patterns matter more than practice.
analyses: A 原句是 motivated me to fix the window，即激励作者自己去修窗，没有说把工作交给工人。
B motivated me to fix the window and become a better handyman 对应鼓励尝试维修、提升动手能力的方向；本句未具体报告维修是否完成或结果如何。
C others 出现在看待自我、他人与世界的概括中，不表示作者放弃维修、转而处理家庭关系。
D 概念拓宽思考范围并不等于把思维和实践排出高低顺序；作者正把修窗作为实际行动的例子。

evidence.quote: My son’s suggestion motivated me to fix the window and become a better handyman

vocabulary.context: 儿子的建议促使作者尝试修窗
vocabulary.example: The challenge motivated her to practise daily.

vocabulary.context: 关于能力是否可以提升的看法
vocabulary.example: Feedback can help students develop a growth mindset.

questions.editorialStatus: 短段版 v2；连续原句，配题片段互不重叠；保留 v1 历史快照，不重算旧成绩
questions.translation: 儿子的建议激励我去修窗户，并努力成为一个更擅长动手维修的人。这是一个小例子，说明成长型思维这样的概念如何拓宽我们看待自我、他人和世界的方式。
questions.promptZh: 儿子的评论对作者产生了什么影响？
optionsZh: 它说服他把维修交给有经验的工人。
它鼓励他尝试亲自动手维修。
它使他的注意力从维修技能转向家庭关系。
它使他相信思维模式比实践更重要。

questions.passage: How, then, is psychological richness different from happiness and meaning? The main body of my book answers this question in detail (see Table 1 for a brief summary). But, very briefly, happiness is a subjective feeling that rises and falls to indicate where one’s life stands. It is a bit like a balloon.
questions.prompt: Which feature of happiness is introduced by the balloon comparison?
options: It steadily grows as a person's experiences accumulate.
It supplies a stable purpose that gives life direction.
It reflects the variety of experiences a person collects.
It fluctuates as a subjective feeling about one's life.
questions.promptZh: 气球的比较首先引出了幸福的哪种特征？
optionsZh: 它随着个人经历的积累而稳定增长。
它提供赋予人生方向的稳定目的。
它反映个人积累的经历有多丰富多样。
它是一种关于自身生活、会起伏的主观感受。
analyses: A steadily grows 与原文 rises and falls 不同；起伏不能改成稳定单向增长。
B 当前片段把 happiness 定义为 subjective feeling，没有把它定义为稳定的人生目的。
C 当前定义强调生活处境的主观感受及其起伏，没有用经历的多样性来界定幸福。
D subjective feeling that rises and falls 直接支持这一改写；气球用于说明起落的特征。

evidence.quote: happiness is a subjective feeling that rises and falls to indicate where one’s life stands. It is a bit like a balloon.

vocabulary.context: 幸福被描述为个人感受到的状态，而非客观财富总数
vocabulary.example: Comfort is partly a subjective judgement.

questions.translation: 那么，心理丰富与幸福和意义有什么不同？本书主体会详细回答这个问题，表 1 则提供简要总结。不过，简而言之，幸福是一种会上下起伏、反映人生当前处境的主观感受。它有点像气球。

questions.passage: Tolstoy was happy and productive. Yet, without any obvious loss, he had a sudden existential crisis at about the age of fifty (years after the publication of War and Peace): “I had a good wife who loved me and whom I loved; good children and a large property which was increasing with no pains taken on my part. I was more respected by my kinsfolk and acquaintance than I had ever been; I was loaded with praise by strangers; and without exaggeration I could believe my name already famous…. And yet I could give no reasonable meaning to any actions of my life.”
questions.prompt: What does Tolstoy’s example suggest within this discussion?
options: Success and affection need not ensure meaning.
A loss of public recognition triggered his crisis.
His productive work supplied a stable sense of purpose.
His family relationships weakened before his crisis began.
analyses: A 他有相爱的妻子、孩子、财产和赞誉，却仍无法为人生行动赋予合理意义。这是个案支持的有限概括：这些条件未必保证意义感。
B 引述说明他得到比以往更多的尊重与赞誉，没有报告失去公众认可，更没有确立这种因果。
C happy and productive 与末句无法赋予意义形成反差，不能把工作多产改成意义感稳定。
D 引述描述相爱的夫妻关系和好孩子，没有报告危机前家庭关系恶化。

evidence.quote: Tolstoy was happy and productive.

Yet, without any obvious loss, he had a sudden existential crisis at about the age of fifty (years after the publication of War and Peace): “I had a good wife who loved me and whom I loved; good children and a large property which was increasing with no pains taken on my part.
And yet I could give no reasonable meaning to any actions of my life.

vocabulary.meaning: 存在危机；对人生意义的深刻疑问
vocabulary.context: 外在生活顺利时仍出现的意义危机
vocabulary.example: The novel follows a writer facing an existential crisis.

questions.editorialStatus: 短段版 v2；连续原句，配题片段互不重叠；保留 v1 历史快照，不重算旧成绩
questions.translation: 托尔斯泰曾幸福而多产。然而，在没有明显损失的情况下，他在大约五十岁时，也就是《战争与和平》出版多年后，突然经历存在危机：“我有一个爱我、我也爱的好妻子；有好孩子，还有一大片无需我费力就不断增值的地产。我比以往更受亲友尊敬，陌生人对我赞誉有加；毫不夸张地说，我相信自己的名字已经出名……然而，我却无法为自己人生中的任何行动赋予合理意义。”
questions.promptZh: 在这段讨论中，托尔斯泰的例子说明什么？
optionsZh: 成功和亲密关爱未必能保证意义感。
失去公众认可引发了他的危机。
多产的工作为他提供了稳定的目标感。
他的家庭关系在危机开始前已经恶化。

questions.passage: Psychological richness is different from happiness and meaning in the sense that it is not about an overall feeling of where life is going or what the point of your life is, but about an experience, or more precisely the accumulation of experiences over time. In the same way that material richness can be quantified by money—the more money you have, the richer you are materially—psychological richness can be quantified by experiences. The more interesting experiences and stories you have, the more psychologically rich you are.
questions.prompt: What distinguishes psychological richness in this passage?
options: The gradual accumulation of interesting experiences.
A current feeling of satisfaction with one's life.
Commitment to a coherent purpose throughout one's life.
The financial wealth spent on unusual experiences.
questions.promptZh: 本段用什么特征区分心理丰富？
optionsZh: 有趣经历随着时间逐渐积累。
对自己当前生活感到满意。
一生致力于一个连贯的目标。
为了不同寻常的经历而花费的财力。
analyses: A the accumulation of experiences over time 与末句 interesting experiences and stories 直接支持以有趣经历的积累区分心理丰富。
B 作者用 not about an overall feeling 排除把它直接等同于人生总体感受，不能改为当前满意感。
C what the point of your life is 被列为与心理丰富不同的关注方向，不能把它重新定义为坚持单一目的。
D money 在本段用于类比 material richness，心理丰富对应的是经历，不是为经历花了多少钱。

evidence.quote: it is not about an overall feeling of where life is going or what the point of your life is, but about an experience, or more precisely the accumulation of experiences over time.
The more interesting experiences and stories you have, the more psychologically rich you are.

vocabulary.context: 作者把经历与金钱作类比，说明丰富可以累积，并未在此提供统一计分公式
vocabulary.example: The benefits cannot always be quantified in a single number.

questions.translation: 心理丰富不同于幸福和意义：它关注的不是人生走向的总体感受，也不是人生的目的，而是经历，更准确地说，是随着时间累积的经历。正如物质丰富可以用金钱量化——钱越多，物质上越富有——心理丰富也可以用经历来量化。有趣的经历和故事越多，心理上就越丰富。
questions.editorialStatus: 按第 1 章 PDF 第 9–16 页具体原文编写；保持已发布短段边界；区分叙事、研究概括、比喻与引文

questions.passage: At bottom, these simpletons want a single thing most of all: that nobody should hurt them. Thus they try to please and gratify everybody. This, however, is cowardice, even if it be called virtue.”
questions.prompt: In the quoted passage, why is pleasing everybody criticised?
options: It enables conventional virtue to challenge their desire for safety.
It places moral independence above their wish for approval.
It is motivated by fear of being hurt.
It makes accepting danger more important than gaining approval.
analyses: A 原文说这些人最想不受伤害，因此讨好众人，并将其批评为怯懦；没有说他们用美德挑战求安全的愿望。
B nobody should hurt them 后接 Thus they try to please，说明动机是避免受伤，不是坚持独立的道德立场。
C nobody should hurt them 与 Thus 形成清楚的动机关系；cowardice 是引述对这种讨好的评价，而不是研究的实验结论。
D 接受危险并不是当前片段给出的讨好动机；它与避免受伤的愿望方向相反。

evidence.quote: At bottom, these simpletons want a single thing most of all: that nobody should hurt them. Thus they try to please and gratify everybody. This, however, is cowardice, even if it be called virtue.

vocabulary.context: 尼采引述中为避免受伤而迎合众人的行为
vocabulary.example: The result will gratify the supporters.

vocabulary.context: 引述质疑被称作美德的怯懦与迎合
vocabulary.example: Patience is a virtue worth practising.

questions.editorialStatus: 短段版 v2；连续原句，配题片段互不重叠；保留 v1 历史快照，不重算旧成绩
questions.translation: 归根结底，这些愚人最渴望的只有一件事：没有人伤害他们。因此，他们试着讨好、取悦所有人。然而这就是怯懦，即使它被称作美德。
questions.promptZh: 在所引片段中，为什么批评取悦所有人？
optionsZh: 它让传统美德挑战他们寻求安全的愿望。
它把道德独立置于获得认可的愿望之上。
它出于害怕受到伤害的动机。
它让接受危险比获得认可更重要。

questions.passage: Well, the bad news is that those who got tenure were not as happy as the current assistant professors imagined.
questions.prompt: What comparison does this sentence make?
options: Tenured professors were less happy than colleagues denied tenure.
Post-tenure happiness fell short of assistant professors' expectations.
Assistant professors expected tenure to lower their own happiness.
Tenure recipients became less happy than before their appointments.
questions.promptZh: 这句话作了什么比较？
optionsZh: 获终身教职者比未获终身教职的同事更不幸福。
获得终身教职后的幸福程度低于助理教授的预想。
助理教授预期获得终身教职会降低自己的幸福程度。
终身教职获得者比获得该职位前更不幸福。
analyses: A 本句比较实际幸福与 current assistant professors 的预想，不是在比较获得与未获得终身教职的两组人。
B not as happy as ... imagined 表明实际幸福程度低于预想；较低于预期不等于绝对不幸福。
C 原句报告获得者没有预想得那么幸福，没有说预测者原本预期会下降。
D 前后实际变化与实际对照预期是不同的比较，本句没有提供同一批人任职前后的幸福数据。

evidence.quote: those who got tenure were not as happy as the current assistant professors imagined.

vocabulary.context: 修饰预测的幸福程度，区别实际经历
vocabulary.example: The course was more demanding than she had imagined.

questions.translation: 那么，坏消息是，获得终身教职的人，并没有现任助理教授想象的那么幸福。

questions.passage: They were given an empty envelope for any stickers they wanted to donate to an anonymous classmate. After the session was over, the researcher counted how many stickers each child donated as a behavioral measure of altruistic giving. Before the earthquake, nine-year-olds gave, on average, slightly more than one out of the ten stickers. One month after the earthquake, nine-year-olds gave, on average, about four out of the ten stickers.
questions.prompt: What served as the behavioural measure of altruistic giving?
questions.promptZh: 什么被用作利他给予的行为测量？
options: The number of stickers still displayed in the original set of one hundred.
The number of stickers each child actually donated, counted after the session.
Only the child's claim that they were generous, without counting donations.
The number of classmates who had not been selected, regardless of what the child gave.
optionsZh: 原来一百张中仍在展示的数量。
结束后数每名儿童实际捐出的贴纸数量。
只听儿童自称慷慨，不数捐赠。
未被选中同学的数量，不管儿童实际给多少。
analyses: A 测量的是每名儿童实际捐出的贴纸数，不是原始展示的一百张还剩多少。
B after the session was over、counted how many stickers 和 each child donated 共同说明测量时点、动作和对象。
C behavioral measure 在这里通过实际捐赠行为取得，不是只询问儿童是否自认慷慨。
D 未获选同学的人数不是每名儿童的捐赠量；捐出的贴纸数量才是本题所问的指标。

vocabulary.meaning: 行为测量；以实际行为数量等作为指标
vocabulary.context: 此处贴纸捐出数是操作性指标，不穷尽一个人的全部道德品格。
vocabulary.example: The number of items donated was used as a behavioral measure.
collocations: a behavioral measure of altruistic giving
counted how many stickers each child donated

questions.translation: 他们拿空信封，装想捐给一名匿名同学的贴纸。结束后，研究者数捐出数量，作为利他给予的行为测量。震前九岁儿童平均捐十张中略多于一张；震后一月平均约四张。

evidence.quote: After the session was over, the researcher counted how many stickers each child donated as a behavioral measure of altruistic giving.

questions.passage: Why so down on happiness? One common critique is that a happy life might be a selfish one. In reality, there is lots of evidence that suggests otherwise. For example, spending money on others as opposed to on oneself increases happiness.
questions.prompt: How does the spending example relate to the critique of happiness?
options: It shows how self-directed spending explains generosity to others.
It challenges the proposed link between happiness and selfishness.
It treats the two kinds of spending as equally effective.
It presents personal financial gain as the basis of happiness.
questions.promptZh: 花钱的例子与对幸福的批评是什么关系？
optionsZh: 它说明为自己花钱如何解释对他人的慷慨。
它对把幸福与自私相联系的批评提出质疑。
它把两种花钱方式视为同样有效。
它把个人财务收益视为幸福的基础。
analyses: A 例子的支出对象是 others，与 on oneself 对照，并没有用自我导向的消费来解释慷慨。
B otherwise 引出反向证据：为别人花钱也与幸福增加相联系。这里挑战的是批评所提出的联系，不把 might 偷换为必然自私，也不声称任何幸福的人都不可能自私。
C as opposed to 表示支出对象的对比，当前句没有报告两种方式效果相同。
D 例子说的是把钱花给谁，不是个人赚到更多钱；不能把支出对象换成财务收益。

evidence.quote: One common critique is that a happy life might be a selfish one. In reality, there is lots of evidence that suggests otherwise.
spending money on others as opposed to on oneself increases happiness.

vocabulary.context: 在此对比消费的受益者：别人和自己
vocabulary.example: The session focuses on practice as opposed to theory.

questions.translation: 为什么如此贬低幸福？一种常见批评认为，幸福的生活可能是自私的生活。实际上，有大量证据指向相反的情况。例如，把钱花在别人身上而不是自己身上，会增加幸福感。

questions.passage: Happy people volunteer more than unhappy people. But, for now, let’s assume the critique of happiness-as-selfishness and proceed with a question: What makes for a good life, if not happiness?
questions.prompt: Why does the author temporarily assume the happiness-as-selfishness critique?
options: To set aside the evidence about volunteering as unreliable.
To investigate whether selfish behaviour produces lasting happiness.
To replace a question about good lives with one about generosity.
To consider sources of a good life beyond happiness.
questions.promptZh: 作者为什么暂时接受“幸福即自私”的批评作假定？
optionsZh: 把关于志愿服务的证据视为不可靠而搁置。
调查自私行为能否产生持久幸福。
用关于慷慨的问题替代关于美好生活的问题。
考察幸福之外构成美好生活的来源。
analyses: A for now, let’s assume 是暂时采用一种讨论前提，不表示认定志愿服务证据不可靠。
B 随后的问题是 What makes for a good life, if not happiness，并非自私行为能否制造持久幸福。
C 作者保留了关于美好生活的问题，只是暂时把幸福放在一边，并未把问题替换成如何慷慨。
D proceed with a question 后直接问如果不是幸福，什么构成美好生活，说明这样设定是为了展开其他可能性。

evidence.quote: for now, let’s assume the critique of happiness-as-selfishness and proceed with a question: What makes for a good life, if not happiness?

vocabulary.context: 这里为动词，比较志愿服务多寡，不是职业名称
vocabulary.example: I volunteer at the community garden on Saturdays.

questions.translation: 幸福的人比不幸福的人做更多志愿服务。不过，目前先让我们接受“幸福就是自私”这一批评作为假定，接着问：如果不是幸福，什么能构成美好生活？

questions.passage: But if you are not making any positive difference in the world, your life may feel pointless. Likewise, a meaningless life has no clear purpose. People without a clear purpose tend to go through their lives aimlessly. Finally, a meaningless life feels torn and highly fragmented.
questions.prompt: Which combination characterises the meaningless life described here?
options: Strong positive impact, unclear purpose, and fragmented experience.
No positive impact, a clear purpose, and fragmented experience.
No positive impact, unclear purpose, and fragmented experience.
No positive impact, unclear purpose, and an integrated life.
questions.promptZh: 哪组特征概括这里描述的无意义生活？
optionsZh: 强烈的正面影响、不明确的目的和破碎的体验。
没有正面影响、目的明确和破碎的体验。
没有正面影响、目的不明确和破碎的体验。
没有正面影响、目的不明确和整合成一体的生活。
analyses: A not making any positive difference 与 strong positive impact 不符；另外两项相似也不能使整组成立。
B no clear purpose 与 a clear purpose 方向相反。
C 三项分别对应 not making any positive difference、no clear purpose 和 torn and highly fragmented；这是当前片段描述的特征组合，不是对每个人作诊断。
D an integrated life 与 highly fragmented 相反，把整体感这一项颠倒了。

evidence.quote: if you are not making any positive difference in the world, your life may feel pointless.
a meaningless life has no clear purpose.
a meaningless life feels torn and highly fragmented.

vocabulary.context: 描述缺乏清晰目标时生活的走向，不是空间上迷路
vocabulary.example: He spent the afternoon wandering aimlessly.

questions.translation: 但如果你没有给世界带来任何正面影响，你的人生可能会让你觉得毫无意义。同样，无意义的生活没有明确目的。没有明确目的的人往往漫无目标地度过人生。最后，无意义的生活让人感到撕裂、极为破碎。

questions.passage: Needless to say, a meaningful life sounds a lot more appealing than a meaningless one. Thus, people say you should find a reason for living— whether via career, religion, social roles (e.g., parenthood), scientific discovery, or social change. Many commencement speakers preach along these lines, including Michelle Obama in her speech to CUNY’s class of 2016: “Be great. Build great lives for yourselves….
questions.prompt: Which statement accurately reflects the routes to a reason for living listed here?
options: Career, religion, social rank, scientific discovery, and social change.
Career, religion, parenthood, income growth, and scientific discovery.
Religion, parenthood, scientific discovery, personal fame, and social change.
Career, religion, social roles, scientific discovery, and social change.
questions.promptZh: 哪一项准确反映这里列举的人生理由的来源？
optionsZh: 事业、宗教、社会等级、科学发现和社会变革。
事业、宗教、为人父母、收入增长和科学发现。
宗教、为人父母、科学发现、个人名气和社会变革。
事业、宗教、社会角色、科学发现和社会变革。
analyses: A social roles 指社会角色，不能替换为社会等级 social rank；其余词相同也掩盖不了这一错配。
B parenthood 是社会角色的例子，但 income growth 不在本段清单中。
C personal fame 不在所列途径中；列举人物演讲也不等于把出名设为途径。
D 五项与 whether via 后的并列清单逐项对应。whether ... or 列出可能来源，不要求每个人同时走完所有途径。

evidence.quote: whether via career, religion, social roles (e.g., parenthood), scientific discovery, or social change.

vocabulary.context: commencement speakers 指毕业典礼演讲者，此处不是项目开工者
vocabulary.example: She was invited to give a commencement address.

questions.translation: 不用说，有意义的生活听起来比无意义的生活更有吸引力。因此，人们说你应该找到活着的理由——可以通过事业、宗教、社会角色（如为人父母）、科学发现或社会变革来寻找。许多毕业典礼演讲者都作过类似劝勉，包括 Michelle Obama 在纽约市立大学 2016 届毕业典礼上的话：“成就伟大。为你们自己建立出色的人生……”

questions.passage: Dr. Donna Adams-Pickett did exactly what Michele Obama promoted. As a child, she learned that her paternal grandmother, who lived on a tobacco farm, died while giving birth. The baby died as well, and her father was left motherless at age twelve. After hearing this story, she was determined to become an ob-gyn doctor.
questions.prompt: What event led Donna Adams-Pickett to decide to become an ob-gyn doctor?
options: Learning that her father had chosen medicine after losing his mother.
Discovering that her grandmother had worked in maternal healthcare.
Hearing about her grandmother's and the baby's deaths in childbirth.
Experiencing her own mother's death while she was twelve years old.
questions.promptZh: 什么事件促使 Donna Adams-Pickett 决定成为妇产科医生？
optionsZh: 得知父亲在失去母亲后选择了从医。
发现祖母曾从事孕产妇医疗照护。
听到祖母与婴儿在分娩中去世的故事。
自己十二岁时经历了母亲去世。
analyses: A 原文说父亲十二岁失去母亲，决定成为妇产科医生的是 Donna，不能把职业选择移给父亲。
B tobacco farm 是祖母的生活地点，没有说祖母在孕产医疗领域工作。
C 祖母分娩时去世，婴儿也死亡；After hearing this story 直接连接这一家庭故事与 Donna 的从医决心。
D 十二岁失母的是她的父亲，不是 Donna 本人；paternal grandmother 也不能换成她自己的母亲。

evidence.quote: her paternal grandmother, who lived on a tobacco farm, died while giving birth. The baby died as well
After hearing this story, she was determined to become an ob-gyn doctor.

vocabulary.context: paternal grandmother 指父亲的母亲，即祖母
vocabulary.example: His paternal grandfather grew up near the coast.

questions.translation: Donna Adams-Pickett 医生确实践行了 Michele Obama 所提倡的事。小时候，她得知住在烟草农场的祖母在分娩时去世，婴儿也没能活下来，她父亲十二岁就失去了母亲。听到这个故事后，她下定决心成为妇产科医生。

questions.passage: As she shared with PBS NewsHour, Dr. Adams-Pickett delivered over 6,000 babies over the last twenty years in Augusta, Georgia, an area located in a maternity care desert. Her life is certainly meaningful, as she has a clear purpose (provide good maternal care to the people of Georgia, especially Black women, who have a much higher rate of maternal mortality before and after delivery than other women) and significance (some mothers and babies might have died without her care).
questions.prompt: How does the author illustrate significance in Dr. Adams-Pickett’s life?
options: By pointing to the clear professional goal that guides her work.
By noting that her care may have saved mothers and babies.
By explaining how her family history gives her life coherence.
By treating her television interview as evidence of public recognition.
questions.promptZh: 作者怎样说明 Adams-Pickett 医生人生的重要性？
optionsZh: 指出引导她工作的明确职业目标。
指出她的照护可能挽救了母亲与婴儿。
解释她的家族经历如何让人生具有连贯性。
把她的电视采访视为公众认可的证据。
analyses: A clear purpose 是作者在同一句中区分出的目的维度，本题问 significance，不能把两个维度混用。
B significance 后明确写 some mothers and babies might have died without her care。可能避免死亡对应可能挽救生命，保留 some 与 might 的范围，没有声称已确定挽救了每个人。
C 家族经历与连贯性的联系并不是当前句对 significance 给出的解释；本句把重要性落在照护可能带来的生命影响上。
D PBS NewsHour 是叙述的信息出处，不是作者用来界定重要性的指标；出镜也不能自动改写为公众认可。

evidence.quote: significance (some mothers and babies might have died without her care).

vocabulary.meaning: 孕产照护资源匮乏地区
vocabulary.context: 用 desert 比喻照护资源稀少的地区，并非气候沙漠
vocabulary.example: The report describes efforts to serve a maternity care desert.
collocations: live in a maternity care desert

questions.translation: Adams-Pickett 医生向 PBS《新闻时刻》分享说，过去二十年，她在佐治亚州奥古斯塔接生了六千多名婴儿；当地是孕产照护资源匮乏地区。她的人生无疑有意义：有明确目的——为佐治亚居民提供良好孕产照护，尤其关注分娩前后孕产死亡率远高于其他女性的黑人女性；也有重要性——如果没有她的照护，一些母亲与婴儿可能已经死亡。

questions.passage: Like the happiness trap, there is also a meaning trap. The first element of the meaning trap is that the type of accomplishment associated with a meaningful life is so grand that aiming for it will set us up for a failure.
questions.prompt: What is the first element of the meaning trap?
options: Giving up meaningful goals in order to protect one's happiness.
Mistaking a clear sense of purpose for a public achievement.
Expecting such grand accomplishments that failure becomes more likely.
Treating an achieved goal as the end of personal development.
questions.promptZh: 意义陷阱的第一个因素是什么？
optionsZh: 为保护自己的幸福而放弃有意义的目标。
把明确的目的感误当作公开的成就。
期待过于宏大的成就，使自己更容易遭遇失败。
把一个目标的达成视为个人发展的终点。
analyses: A 当前片段指出的是对成就的期待过高，没有说人们为了幸福而放弃目标。
B 问题是把与意义关联的成就设得过于宏大，不是把个人目的感误认成一项公开成就。
C so grand ... aiming for it will set us up for a failure 表达宏大门槛使人处于容易失败的境地；这是一种陷阱的解释，不是每个人都必然失败的统计定律。
D 本段没有讨论达成目标之后停止成长，而是讨论追求过于宏大成就时的困难。

evidence.quote: the type of accomplishment associated with a meaningful life is so grand that aiming for it will set us up for a failure.

vocabulary.meaning: 使我们容易遭遇；使我们陷入
vocabulary.context: 这里指宏大标准使追求者容易落入失败，不是预订安排
vocabulary.example: Unrealistic deadlines can set a team up for failure.

questions.translation: 就像幸福陷阱一样，也存在意义陷阱。意义陷阱的第一个因素是：人们把有意义的生活与过于宏大的成就联系起来，以至于追求那种成就会让自己容易遭遇失败。

questions.passage: In the cleverly entitled paper “Life Is Pretty Meaningful,” Samantha Heintzelman and Laura King report that 90 percent of Americans said they have meaning in life, according to the Gallup World Polls.
questions.prompt: What does the reported 90 percent represent?
options: Americans who said their lives lacked a clear purpose.
People worldwide whose lives the researchers judged meaningful.
Americans selecting the highest purpose score on a five-point scale.
Americans' self-reported meaning in the cited Gallup poll.
questions.promptZh: 这里报告的 90% 代表什么？
optionsZh: 说自己的人生缺少明确目的的美国人。
全世界由研究者判定其人生有意义的人。
在五点量表上选择最高目的感分数的美国人。
所引 Gallup 调查中美国人自报的人生意义感。
analyses: A 原句是 said they have meaning in life，不能改成自报缺乏目的。
B Americans 被扩大成全球人群，said 也被替换成研究者判断，两个范围都不符。
C 当前句没有把 90% 定义为五点量表的最高分组；不能把自报有意义与强烈同意混为同一指标。
D 90 percent of Americans said ... according to the Gallup World Polls 同时确定了人群、自报性质和调查来源。

evidence.quote: 90 percent of Americans said they have meaning in life, according to the Gallup World Polls.

vocabulary.context: 此处为动词，主语是论文作者，结果来自 Gallup 数据
vocabulary.example: The researchers report a difference between the two groups.

questions.translation: Samantha Heintzelman 和 Laura King 在题名巧妙的论文《人生颇有意义》中报告说，根据 Gallup 世界民意调查，90% 的美国人说自己人生有意义。

questions.passage: To say, “No, my life has no purpose nor meaning,” is almost to say one’s life is pointless. Those who did not feel like their lives were utterly pointless were likely to say yes to this question. This means that even if someone did not feel their life was particularly meaningful, they might have said yes.
questions.prompt: Why might someone answer yes without finding life particularly meaningful?
options: The question asks them to rate happiness rather than life meaning.
They understand yes as proof of notable personal achievements.
A no could imply a stronger rejection than they feel.
They mistake the yes-or-no format for a scale of strong agreement.
questions.promptZh: 为什么一个不觉得人生特别有意义的人仍可能回答“是”？
optionsZh: 这个问题让他们评价幸福而不是人生意义。
他们把回答“是”理解为显著个人成就的证明。
回答“否”可能意味着比他们实际感受更强烈的否定。
他们把是非题格式误认为表示强烈同意程度的量表。
analyses: A 当前片段围绕 purpose、meaning 和 pointless 展开，没有把所问内容改成幸福评分。
B 原文没有说回答是认证了显著成就；作者解释的是对 utterly pointless 这一强烈否定的距离。

questions.passage: Psychologist Michael Steger and colleagues asked participants to report how meaningful they feel their lives are. In addition, he asked their friends and family members to report the participant’s meaning in life. If the high percentage of self-reported meaning in life is only an illusion, informant reports would not correlate with self-reports. What he found was different: self-reported meaning in life is correlated with informant-reported meaning in life.
questions.prompt: Which finding challenges the idea that reported meaning is only an illusion?
options: Participants and informants were describing different people's lives.
Participants and informants gave the same average level of meaning.
Self-reports correlated with friends' and relatives' reports.
The meaning reports correlated with participants' income instead.
questions.promptZh: 哪个发现挑战了“自报意义感只是幻觉”的解释？
optionsZh: 参与者和知情人在描述不同人的生活。
参与者和知情人给出的平均意义感水平相同。
自报与朋友和亲属的报告存在相关。
意义感报告与参与者的收入存在相关。
analyses: A 朋友和家人评价的是该参与者的生命意义，不能把双方评定对象改成不同的人。
B 相关描述两组评分如何共同变化，不等于两组平均值相同；原文也没有报告均值相等。
C 原文以 self-reported meaning ... is correlated with informant-reported meaning 对照只是一种幻觉的解释，跨报告者相关是本题所问的发现。
D 本段没有报告收入相关，把知情人报告这个变量换成了收入。

self-reported meaning in life is correlated with informant-reported meaning in life.

vocabulary.context: 这里特指对参与者作评价的朋友和家人，不是警方线人
vocabulary.example: An informant who knew the participant completed the questionnaire.

该测量消除了个人与知情人评分之间的差异。
人格特质直接解释了参与者所报告的人生意义。

B 相关不等于差异被消除，原文没有报告每个参与者与知情人的评分完全一致。
C extraversion 与 neuroticism 在这里是其他研究中测量的特质，用于比较跨报告者相关，不是解释意义感的已证原因。

questions.passage: These personality traits and attitudes express themselves in predictable ways. Others derive meaning in life from their work, family, and community, again a narrowly defined realm of life. Research on meaning in life shows that successfully achieving a meaningful life often comes with focus and narrowness.
questions.prompt: What recurring pattern in finding meaning is described?
options: Exploring new causes is the main way to sustain a sense of meaning.
Work and family provide meaning when combined with volunteering.
Meaningful involvement depends on the size of its public audience.
Meaning is often associated with sustained, focused involvement.

successfully achieving a meaningful life often comes with focus and narrowness.

questions.passage: He gets assigned to a prison housing mostly those suspected of terrorism. He abuses these suspected terrorists, as in the infamous prison abuse case at Abu Ghraib. To question whether he believes he can protect the American people.

questions.passage: So far, the case of Mason, the military prison officer, is merely hypothetical. Is there any scientific evidence for this phenomenon of misplaced meaning in life? Recent studies have found that meaning in life is associated with right-wing authoritarianism, a belief system defined as uncritical submission to authority, feelings of aggression toward those who violate social norms, and strict adherence to conventional values. questions.passage: If you feel like you haven’t made any meaningful difference in the world, consider that you could achieve meaning through devotion to a certain cause, starting out small in your neighborhood. Take your time, and you will make a difference in the long run. The second part of the meaning trap is that the pursuit of a meaningful life can promote a narrow viewpoint. As research shows, meaning in life is sometimes attained through prosocial behaviors toward a small ingroup, and antisocial behaviors or apathy toward outgroups.

questions.passage: Gopnik’s newfound interest in Buddhism provoked a question, one that would lead her down an Alice in Wonderland–esque intellectual rabbit hole. As she read more about Buddhist philosophy, she noticed a similarity in its ideas to David Hume’s Treatise of Human Nature, and she began to wonder if there were Eastern roots in the Western Enlightenment. So began her quest to link Ippolito Desideri, a Jesuit missionary to Tibet who wrote about Buddhism in 1728, with David Hume, who completed his Treatise in 1738.
questions.prompt: What prompted Gopnik’s search for a link between Desideri and Hume?
options: Her discovery that Desideri and Hume attended the same college together.
A prior commitment to show that Hume developed without Eastern ideas.
Similarities she noticed between Buddhist philosophy and Hume's work.
The ten-year gap between the texts by Desideri and Hume.
questions.promptZh: 什么促使 Gopnik 寻找 Desideri 与 Hume 的联系？
optionsZh: 发现Desideri与Hume曾一同在同一学院学习。
事先决意证明Hume的思想发展没有东方影响。
她注意到的佛教哲学与Hume著作之间的相似。
Desideri与Hume两份文本相差十年的时间。
analyses: A 当前片段介绍探究如何开始，没有在此确立两人一同学习的史实。后来的历史线索也不能反填成最初已经证实的动机。
B wonder if 表示开始探索是否存在东方根源，不是事先承诺排除东方影响。
C noticed a similarity 后接 began to wonder 与 quest，明确把阅读中发现的思想相似与寻找联系连接起来。
D 1728与1738是所追索文本的年代背景，句中直接说明的触发点是思想相似，不是仅因相差十年。

D like 引出的地点只是例子，wide range 表明不能把全部价值限于这些首次所见。

questions.passage: The more new conversations you enter, the psychologically richer the party becomes for you. Someone who has a psychologically enriching experience at one party is more likely to go to another party.

B The more new conversations 说明新谈话越多越丰富，不能改成越少。
C more likely 表示可能性较高，不等于以后每场都去的保证。
D 两句分别给出谈话与丰富性、丰富经历与参加另一场聚会的可能性；这是作者所述联系，不把它当作每次聚会的实验因果。

questions.passage: It is interesting to note that Greta Thunberg appears more neurotic than most. She worries intensely about environmental disasters and climate change. However, she seems to leverage her anxiety to fuel her work. So long as one’s neuroticism is not overwhelming, a meaningful life is possible.
questions.prompt: Which reading best respects the caution in the author’s description of Thunberg?
options: Anxiety may fuel her work, in a qualified observation rather than a diagnosis.
Her work demonstrates that anxiety improves performance at any intensity.
A meaningful life is presented as requiring overwhelming anxiety.
The word seems qualifies whether she works, rather than anxiety’s role in it.
questions.promptZh: 哪种理解最保留作者描述 Thunberg 时的谨慎语气？
optionsZh: 焦虑可能推动她的工作；这是有保留的观察，而不是诊断。
她的工作说明任何强度的焦虑都改善表现。
有意义的生活被说成需要压倒性的焦虑。
seems 限定的是她是否工作，而不是焦虑在工作中的作用。
analyses: A appears 和 seems 保留判断余地，本段没有临床诊断材料；not overwhelming 也限制了最后一句的可能性。
B 原文没有任何强度都改善表现的结论，最后一句还明确 not overwhelming。
C 把 not overwhelming 的 not 删除，并把可能条件写成必须有压倒性焦虑，方向相反。
D seems to leverage her anxiety to fuel her work 对焦虑如何推动工作作保留，不是在怀疑她有无工作。

evidence.quote: she seems to leverage her anxiety to fuel her work.
So long as one’s neuroticism is not overwhelming, a meaningful life is possible.

vocabulary.context: 动词，比喻焦虑成为工作动力；作者使用 seems 保留推测
vocabulary.example: Her curiosity helped fuel a long research project.

questions.translation: 值得注意的是，Thunberg 似乎比多数人更具神经质倾向。她强烈担忧环境灾难和气候变化。然而，她似乎把焦虑转化为工作的动力。只要神经质倾向没有强到令人无法承受，有意义的人生仍然可能。

Excessive childhood moves may have lasting well-being costs for introverts who struggle to form connections.
Introverts tend to form new connections more easily after frequent childhood moves.

questions.promptZh: 哪项保留了论文要点的人群与限定？

频繁童年搬迁后，内向者往往更容易建立新联系。
与频繁童年搬迁相关的困难在成年前就会消失。

questions.passage: This question has been at the center of both my personal life and my academic research for decades. His personal life and his academic research.
One brief college decision and no later choices.
optionsZh: 父亲的职业和母亲的学业。

B only 缩小了范围，也把 personal life 排除在外。
C 原文明确并列个人生活与学术研究，并用 for decades 表示持续多年。

questions.passage: There are, of course, trade-offs between a stable life and a mobile life, a simple life and a dramatic life, a comfortable life and a challenging life, a conventional life and an unconventional life. But which one gets us closer to a good life?
questions.prompt: What is the function of the paired alternatives such as “stable” and “mobile”?

To rank all mobile lives as morally superior.
To show that the author has abandoned psychological research.
To demonstrate that all readers have already made the same choice.
analyses: A 成对列举的生活方式带出 trade-offs，最后追问 which...closer to a good life，说明列举用来建立待评估的选择。
B 本片段提出哪种更接近美好生活的问题，未给 mobile 在道德上优越的结论。
C 本片段没有说作者放弃心理研究；提出问题不等于放弃研究。

questions.passage: When author Donna Tartt was asked what questions she was grappling with in her novel The Goldfinch, she said, “What is a good life?…To be happy oneself? Is it personal happiness? Or is it to make other people happy even at the expense of one’s own happiness?” Tartt’s question is profound. Should we strive to be happy? Or should we work for others’ happiness before thinking of our own?
questions.prompt: Why is Donna Tartt’s question included?
options: To prove that self-sacrifice prevents regret.
To report the results of an experiment about generosity.
To frame a tension between personal happiness and making others happy.
To establish that writers reject all forms of happiness.
analyses: A 这里是在问要不要牺牲自己的幸福，没有自我牺牲能避免遗憾的结果或证明。
B 文中引用小说作者对作品问题的回答，不是慷慨行为实验的结果。
C personal happiness 与 make other people happy 的引述，加上作者随后两个 Should 问句，呈现自己与他人幸福的张力。
D 开放问题不是拒绝一切幸福的结论，也不能从一位作家扩大到所有作家。

evidence.quote: Should we strive to be happy? Or should we work for others’ happiness before thinking of our own?

questions.translation: 有人问作家唐娜·塔特，她在小说《金翅雀》中努力探讨什么问题。她说：“什么是美好生活？……让自己幸福吗？是个人幸福吗？还是即使牺牲自己的幸福，也要让别人幸福？”塔特的问题很深刻。我们应该努力让自己幸福吗？还是应该先为他人的幸福努力，再考虑自己的？

As a finding about a proven medical treatment.

questions.passage: A good analogy is dark vs. sweet chocolate. When you eat a fine, dark chocolate, you immediately notice that it is different from a typical, sugary chocolate. It is sweet but also bitter, or even salty. It keeps you surprised, and it has heightened intensity, complexity, and depth. In other words, it’s rich. Likewise, a psychologically rich experience is different from a typical experience; there is something unexpected and powerful. It has a variety of qualities, not just good or bad.
questions.prompt: Why does the author compare psychological richness to dark chocolate?
options: To equate rich experiences with consistently pleasant feelings.
To make lasting richness depend only on immediate intensity.
To rank bitter experiences above every pleasant experience.
To illustrate surprise, complexity and a mixture of qualities.
analyses: A sweet but also bitter, or even salty 及 not just good or bad 不支持始终愉快。
B intensity 与 complexity、depth 并列；only 把丰富性缩减成单一强度，本段也未建立即时强度决定持久丰富性的规则。
C 本段以不同性质的组合解释丰富，不是把一切苦涩都排在一切愉快之上。
D surprised、complexity、depth 以及 variety of qualities 共同说明多层体验的类比，不能只用愉快或不愉快概括。

questions.passage: Over the last two decades, well-being researchers have debated the relative importance of hedonic vs. eudaimonic well-being. The exact number of genes shared by all happy people.
Whether psychology should exclude all accounts of meaningful lives.

所有愉快活动是否带来相同收入。

B 本句没有活动收入或人人收入相同的问题。

questions.passage: Some researchers even claimed to have found different epigenetic patterns between hedonic and eudaimonic well-being, suggesting that our very genes are expressed differently. However, other researchers found that almost all people who say they are happy tend to also say that their lives are meaningful, and vice versa. The overlap between hedonic and eudaimonic well-being is so great that some researchers argue that they are virtually the same thing. Others argue that both happiness and meaning in life are so important that there is no point debating which is more important.
questions.prompt: What is the best summary of the debate described in this paragraph?
options: Researchers unanimously deny that happiness and meaning overlap.
Findings and interpretations differ about the distinction and overlap between happiness and meaning.
The debate has established epigenetic differences beyond dispute.
Acknowledging both dimensions are important means every researcher sees them as identical.
analyses: A 当前段后半正讨论 overlap，unanimously deny 不符合不同研究者的观点。
B Some researchers claimed、other researchers found、some argue 与 Others argue 呈现不同发现和解释，没有统一成单一结论。
C claimed 与 suggesting 是转述和推示，后面还有其他研究及解释，不能改成无争议定论。
D 认为两者都重要、不必争高下，与认为两者相同是不同主张；不能将最后一种观点推广到每位研究者。

The number of links gives an exact formula for a person's happiness.
A single success makes all later illness and danger impossible.

vocabulary.context: 特指想法的出现频率，必须与死亡率所衡量的事件区分。

questions.translation: 根据 CDC 的数据，2020 年发生了 120 万次自杀尝试，以及 1,220 万美国成年人“认真”想过自杀。这意味着当年约每二十名美国成年人中，就有一人认真想过以自杀方式死亡。这个数字很大。因此，若看自杀想法的出现频率，Madison 的个案似乎就没那么罕见了。

evidence.quote: If you look at the frequency of suicidal thoughts, then, Madison’s case doesn’t seem so rare.

questions.passage: At the core of the pressure to be happy is the American cultural construction of happiness as something achievable. In one study, American college students were asked to write about anything that came to mind when they thought about “happiness.” Many wrote something like, “Happiness is a reward for all the hard work you employ” and “Happiness is the feeling of succeeding.” One student wrote simply that happiness is a “victory”!
questions.prompt: What task were the American college students given in the study described?
questions.promptZh: 这项研究让美国大学生完成什么任务？
options: Rank happiness and money on a seven-point scale.
Choose one correct definition from four options.
Record their income before and after graduation.
Write whatever came to mind when thinking about happiness.
optionsZh: 在七点量表上给幸福和金钱排序。
从四个选项中选择一个正确定义。
记录毕业前后的收入。
写下想到幸福时脑海里出现的任何内容。
analyses: A 当前任务是围绕 happiness 写出想到的内容，没有要求用七点量表给金钱与幸福排名。
B anything that came to mind 是开放联想，不是四个固定选项中选一项。
C 当前片段没有收入或毕业前后追踪。
D were asked to write about anything that came to mind 明示写作任务及幸福这个提示词。

vocabulary.context: 让学生围绕幸福自由联想，不是背诵预定答案。
vocabulary.example: When I saw the old photograph, a childhood memory came to mind.
collocations: the first thing that comes to mind

questions.translation: 必须快乐的压力，其核心是美国文化将幸福建构为一种可以实现的东西。在一项研究中，美国大学生被要求写下想到“幸福”时浮现的任何内容。许多人写道，幸福是所有辛勤努力的回报，或幸福是成功时的感受。一名学生干脆把幸福称为一场“胜利”！

evidence.quote: In one study, American college students were asked to write about anything that came to mind when they thought about “happiness.”

questions.passage: The earlier findings were replicated: American college students tend to equate happiness with personal achievement.
questions.prompt: What association was found in the American college students’ responses?
options: Happiness was defined exclusively as inherited wealth.
Students agreed that sadness was a medical diagnosis.
Happiness was often connected with personal achievement.
Happiness was viewed as unrelated to success.
analyses: A 当前句没有将幸福排他地定义为继承的财富。
B 本句没有关于悲伤的医学诊断，也不是在报告诊断调查。
C tend to equate happiness with personal achievement 表示这种倾向；保留美国大学生的样本范围。
D equate happiness with personal achievement 与认为幸福和成功无关相反。

evidence.quote: The earlier findings were replicated: American college students tend to equate happiness with personal achievement.

questions.translation: 较早的发现得到了重复验证：美国大学生倾向于把幸福等同于个人成就。

幸福被视为与成功无关。

questions.passage: What happiness researchers found was quite different from the achievement-oriented concept of happiness; a victory rarely results in everlasting (or even long-lasting) happiness. The effect of a major accomplishment like a promotion on happiness seems to disappear within six months.
questions.prompt: What qualification does the passage make about happiness after a major accomplishment?
options: Its effect seems to disappear within six months.
Its effect is guaranteed to last for life.
Every accomplishment immediately reduces happiness.
Promotions affect happiness only after six months have passed.
questions.promptZh: 本段怎样限定重大成就带来的幸福？
optionsZh: 其影响似乎会在六个月内消失。
其影响被保证持续一生。
每项成就都会立刻降低幸福感。
晋升只会在六个月过去后才开始影响幸福。
analyses: A seems to disappear within six months 同时保留似乎和六个月内，不能换成固定恰在第六个月。

evidence.quote: The effect of a major accomplishment like a promotion on happiness seems to disappear within six months.

vocabulary.context: 本段否定胜利通常会带来永久幸福的期待

questions.translation: 幸福研究者的发现与成就导向的幸福观很不一样：一次胜利很少带来永久的，甚至长期的幸福。像晋升这样的重大成就对幸福的影响，似乎会在六个月内消失。

questions.passage: If you are unhappy, you are a loser. The pressure to be happy might come from this cultural narrative of happiness as a sign of success. In Saul Steinberg’s iconic 1959 New Yorker cover, Prosperity wins the contest of the Pursuit of Happiness, suggesting that it takes success and prosperity to be happy.
questions.prompt: How is Steinberg’s magazine cover used here?
options: As experimental proof that prosperity guarantees happiness.
As an illustration of a cultural story linking happiness with success.
As evidence that the author endorses calling unhappy people losers.
As a record of who won a real happiness competition.
questions.promptZh: Steinberg 的杂志封面在这里起什么作用？
optionsZh: 作为富裕保证幸福的实验证据。
展示把幸福与成功相联的文化叙事。
证明作者赞同把不幸福者称为失败者。
记录一场真实幸福比赛的获胜者。
analyses: A 封面是文化例证，不是因果实验。
B cultural narrative 与封面上 Prosperity 获胜的形象呼应。
C 文段在说明压力来源，不能把被描述的标签当成作者赞同。
D 把象征性封面误读成实际比赛记录。

In Saul Steinberg’s iconic 1959 New Yorker cover, Prosperity wins the contest of the Pursuit of Happiness, suggesting that it takes success and prosperity to be happy.

vocabulary.context: 指文化中幸福象征成功的故事或理解方式
vocabulary.example: The film challenges a familiar narrative about success.

questions.translation: 按照这里描述的文化叙事，如果你不幸福，你就是个“失败者”。必须幸福的压力，也许来自这种把幸福看作成功标志的文化叙事。Saul Steinberg 那幅具有代表性的 1959 年《纽约客》封面上，“富裕”赢得“追求幸福”的竞赛，暗示必须成功而富裕才能幸福。

questions.passage: If you are unhappy, you are a loser. The pressure to be happy might come from this cultural narrative of happiness as a sign of success. questions.passage: Decades of research on the “affective forecasting error” suggest that we tend to overestimate the happiness that our success will bring about, while also overestimating the unhappiness that our failure will generate.
questions.prompt: What is the affective forecasting error described in the passage?
options: Accurately predicting lasting happiness from every success.
Predicting both success-related joy and failure-related distress as greater than they turn out to be.
Underestimating the value of every possible promotion.
Expecting failure to make people happier than success.
analyses: A suggest that we tend to overestimate 说明预测偏高的倾向，不是每次都能准确预测。
B 同时保留高估成功带来的幸福与高估失败带来的不幸福两侧；suggest、tend 不等于所有人每次都如此。
C underestimating 把高估方向反转，原句也没有每次晋升价值的评价。
D 高估失败带来的不幸福，不等于预期失败比成功更快乐。

evidence.quote: Decades of research on the “affective forecasting error” suggest that we tend to overestimate the happiness that our success will bring about, while also overestimating the unhappiness that our failure will generate.

vocabulary.context: 对成功和失败带来的情绪强度预测偏高
vocabulary.example: We often overestimate how much we can do in a day.

questions.editorialStatus: 短段版 v2；连续原句，配题片段互不重叠；保留 v1 历史快照，不重算旧成绩
questions.translation: 数十年关于“情感预测偏差”的研究表明，我们往往高估成功会带来的幸福，同时也高估失败将造成的不幸福。
questions.promptZh: 片段所述的情感预测偏差是什么？
optionsZh: 准确预测每次成功带来的持久幸福。
把成功的喜悦和失败的痛苦都预测得比实际更强烈。
低估每一种可能晋升的价值。
预期失败会比成功使人更幸福。

questions.passage: The good news is that those who were denied tenure were far happier than the current assistant professors imagined.
questions.prompt: How did those denied tenure compare with current assistant professors’ expectations?
options: They refused to discuss their happiness.
They were far happier than current assistant professors had imagined.
They were guaranteed to become happier than all tenured professors.
They were exactly as devastated as predicted.
analyses: A 当前句报告幸福感比较，没有拒绝交流的信息。
B far happier than...imagined 保留幸福得多及现任助理教授的想象这一比较基准。
C 原句不是与所有已获终身教职者比较，也没有 guaranteed 的保证。
D far happier than imagined 与恰好同预测一样痛苦相反。

evidence.quote: The good news is that those who were denied tenure were far happier than the current assistant professors imagined.

vocabulary.context: 助理教授预测获得或未获终身教职的情绪

questions.translation: 好消息是，那些未获终身教职的人，比现任助理教授想象的要幸福得多。
questions.promptZh: 未获终身教职者的幸福感，与现任助理教授的预期相比怎样？
optionsZh: 他们拒绝谈论自己的幸福感。
他们比现任助理教授原先想象的幸福得多。
他们被保证会比所有获得终身教职的教授更幸福。
他们与预测一样遭受沉重打击。

questions.passage: Happiness is the frequency, not the intensity, of positive events. Relatedly, studies show that happiness is the product of close relationships rather than personal accomplishments. That is, happiness is not personal success, but interpersonal success.
questions.prompt: Which emphasis on happiness is expressed in this passage?
options: One sufficiently intense personal achievement.
Frequent positive events and close relationships.
Frequent public recognition of individual success.
Avoiding every form of social interaction.
analyses: A frequency, not intensity 与 rather than personal accomplishments 不支持仅靠一次强烈个人成就。
B 直接概括积极事件频率和 close relationships，不增加当前三句未写出的事件大小。
C frequent 只保留频率，却将亲密关系偷换成公众认可和个人成功。
D avoiding social interaction 与 close relationships 及 interpersonal success 相反。

evidence.quote: Happiness is the frequency, not the intensity, of positive events.
Relatedly, studies show that happiness is the product of close relationships rather than personal accomplishments.

vocabulary.context: 与积极事件的发生频率形成对照
vocabulary.example: The intensity of the light changed slowly.

questions.translation: 幸福在于积极事件的频率，而非强度。相关研究还显示，幸福是亲密关系的产物，而非个人成就的产物。也就是说，幸福不在于个人成功，而在于人际成功。
questions.promptZh: 这段对幸福强调了什么？
optionsZh: 一次足够强烈的个人成就。
频繁的积极事件与亲密关系。
经常获得针对个人成功的公众认可。
避免一切形式的社交互动。

questions.passage: The first insight from the science of happiness is that people overestimate the role of success in their own happiness. The joy of a big promotion, marriage, or a first child is relatively short-lived. It is not a big win that brings happiness. Rather, it’s the small things in life, like having a coffee with your best friend every day, that build long-term happiness.
questions.prompt: What is the first insight the author draws from happiness research?
questions.promptZh: 作者从幸福研究中概括出的第一个认识是什么？
options: Success is the only possible source of happiness.
People underestimate every effect of failure.
People exaggerate the role of success in their happiness.
All personal achievements have exactly zero emotional effect.
optionsZh: 成功是幸福唯一可能的来源。
人们低估了失败的每一种影响。
人们夸大了成功在自身幸福中的作用。
所有个人成就都恰好没有任何情绪作用。
analyses: A overestimate the role of success 是对高估成功作用的批评，不是确认唯一来源。
B 目标句讲成功的作用，不是失败的每一种影响。
C exaggerate 对应 overestimate，role 保留作用范围，不能扩大成唯一决定因素。
D 高估并不表示实际作用恰好为零，all 和 exactly 均扩大原句。

vocabulary.context: 估计成功对幸福的作用过大，而不是说成功完全无效。
vocabulary.example: We may overestimate how much time a simple task will require.

questions.translation: 幸福科学的第一个启示是，人们高估了成功在自身幸福中的作用。重大晋升、结婚或第一个孩子出生的喜悦，都相对短暂。带来幸福的不是一次大胜。相反，生活中的小事，比如每天和最好的朋友喝杯咖啡，才会积累长期幸福。

evidence.quote: The first insight from the science of happiness is that people overestimate the role of success in their own happiness.

questions.passage: So why do people fake happiness? There is, of course, the saying “Fake it till you make it.” Many people take to heart the belief that if you continue to pretend you are successful, you will eventually succeed.
questions.prompt: What issue does the opening question about faking happiness introduce?
questions.promptZh: So why do people fake happiness? 引出了什么问题？
options: How to measure the memory of a mobile phone.
Whether all happiness research should be abandoned.
Why people present happiness that they may not actually feel.
How to prove that every happy person is pretending.
optionsZh: 如何测量手机内存。
是否应放弃所有幸福研究。
人们为何呈现自己可能并未真正感到的幸福。
如何证明每个幸福的人都在伪装。
analyses: A 当前问句主题是 people fake happiness，没有提出手机内存测量的问题。
B 本句没有提出放弃全部幸福研究。

D 询问人们为什么假装，并不能推出每个看起来幸福的人都在假装。

questions.translation: 那么，人们为什么假装幸福？当然，有句俗话叫“先装得像，直到真的做到”。许多人深信，如果持续装作成功，最终就会成功。

evidence.quote: So why do people fake happiness?

questions.translation: 那么，人们为什么假装幸福？当然，有句俗话叫“先装得像，直到真的做到”。许多人深信，如果持续装作成功，最终就会成功。

evidence.quote: There is, of course, the saying “Fake it till you make it.”

questions.editorialStatus: 逐题作者稿；已核对实际PDF原页；定位到此前未直接配题的候选句，不改写原句、不把上下文当作直接证据。

questions.passage: Quentin Tarantino, who went on to write and direct the iconic film Pulp Fiction among others, was working as a clerk at a video store in Manhattan Beach, California, when, in order to get his first Hollywood job as a production assistant, he lied, saying that he had worked in the movie industry. Steve Jobs faked it till he made it, too. The first iPhone had a memory problem. It could not run multiple programs simultaneously.
questions.prompt: According to the account, why did Tarantino claim previous film-industry experience?
questions.promptZh: 按书中叙述，塔伦蒂诺为何声称自己有电影行业经历？
options: To explain why he refused to leave the video store.
To secure his first Hollywood job as a production assistant.
To demonstrate that he had already directed every major film.
To persuade researchers to include him in a happiness experiment.
optionsZh: 解释自己为何拒绝离开录像店。
为得到在好莱坞担任制作助理的第一份工作。
证明自己已经执导所有重要电影。
说服研究者把他纳入幸福实验。
analyses: A 录像店工作是当时背景，目的条款并不是说他拒绝离开。
B in order to get his first Hollywood job as a production assistant 直接给出他所说谎言的目的。
C went on to write and direct 是后来的经历，不等于当时已导演所有重要作品。
D 当前句是职业经历叙述，没有心理实验招募信息；也不能从一个故事推出所有人这样做都能获益。

vocabulary.context: 他希望得到的第一份好莱坞职位，不是其后来导演身份。
vocabulary.example: The production assistant helped organise the filming schedule.
collocations: a job as a production assistant

questions.translation: Quentin Tarantino 后来编剧并执导了《低俗小说》等知名电影；当时他在加利福尼亚州曼哈顿海滩一家录像店做店员。为了获得第一份好莱坞制片助理工作，他谎称曾在电影业工作。Steve Jobs 也是先装得像，直到真正做到。第一代 iPhone 有内存问题，无法同时运行多个程序。

evidence.quote: Quentin Tarantino, who went on to write and direct the iconic film Pulp Fiction among others, was working as a clerk at a video store in Manhattan Beach, California, when, in order to get his first Hollywood job as a production assistant, he lied, saying that he had worked in the movie industry.

questions.editorialStatus: 逐题作者稿；已核对实际PDF原页；定位到此前未直接配题的候选句，不改写原句、不把上下文当作直接证据。

questions.passage: So, when the iPhone onstage had a poor connection, they faked it and consistently showed five bars of signal. Eventually, Apple fixed the memory problem. Likewise, might many Americans assume that, if they pretend to be happy, they will eventually become happy?
questions.prompt: Which problem does the passage say Apple eventually fixed?
questions.promptZh: 原文说苹果最终修复了什么问题？
options: The onstage phone’s poor connection.
The memory problem.
The practice of displaying five signal bars.
Every fault affecting the demonstration.
optionsZh: 台上手机的连接不佳问题。
内存问题。
显示五格信号的做法。
影响演示的每一种故障。
analyses: A 文中先写连接不佳时伪装信号显示，后来明确说修复的是 memory problem，没有说修好该连接。
B Eventually, Apple fixed the memory problem 直接给出最终修复的对象。
C 始终显示五格是掩盖连接状况的做法，没有被说成后来修复的技术问题。
D 只明确说内存问题被修好，不能扩大成演示中每一种故障均已修复。

vocabulary.context: 交代案例中的后续解决，不保证先假装就必然解决所有问题。
vocabulary.example: After several revisions, the team eventually solved the problem.

questions.translation: 因此，当台上的 iPhone 连接不佳时，他们作了假，始终显示五格信号。后来，苹果修复了内存问题。同样地，许多美国人是否也会以为，只要假装幸福，最终就会真的幸福呢？

evidence.quote: Eventually, Apple fixed the memory problem.

questions.editorialStatus: 逐题作者稿；已核对实际PDF原页；定位到此前未直接配题的候选句，不改写原句、不把上下文当作直接证据。

questions.passage: We don’t know definitively whether most Americans assume pretending to be happy will make them happy. Even so, there is a famous experiment in which participants held a pen in their mouth so as to mimic either smiling or not smiling. They then saw several cartoons and rated how funny they were. What the researchers found was quite striking.
questions.prompt: What uncertainty does the author explicitly acknowledge?
questions.promptZh: 作者明确承认了哪项不确定性？
options: Whether participants were asked to rate how funny cartoons were.
Whether mimicking a smile necessarily meant feeling genuinely happy.
Whether the pen was held in the mouth during the task.
Whether most Americans believe pretending to be happy will make them happy.
optionsZh: 是否要求参与者评价漫画有多好笑。
模仿微笑是否必然意味着内心真的快乐。
任务中笔是否含在嘴里。
多数美国人是否相信假装幸福会让自己变幸福。
analyses: A They then saw...rated 明确给出任务，不是作者点名尚无定论的群体信念。
B 模仿表情与真实感受不同，但作者明确承认的未知是多数美国人持什么看法，不是本项的必然关系。
C held a pen in their mouth 已明确交代操作。
D don’t know definitively whether most Americans assume...准确给出未知对象；未知不能改写成所有人都相信或都不相信。

vocabulary.context: don’t know definitively 承认没有确定答案，不是证明该信念必然真或假。
vocabulary.example: The small survey could not answer the question definitively.

questions.translation: 我们并不能确定，多数美国人是否认为假装幸福就会使自己幸福。即便如此，有一个著名实验，让参与者嘴里叼着笔，以模拟微笑或不微笑。随后，他们观看几幅漫画，并评价其好笑程度。研究者的发现相当惊人。

evidence.quote: We don’t know definitively whether most Americans assume pretending to be happy will make them happy.

questions.editorialStatus: 逐题作者稿；已核对实际PDF原页；定位到此前未直接配题的候选句，不改写原句、不把上下文当作直接证据。

questions.passage: We don’t know definitively whether most Americans assume pretending to be happy will make them happy. Even so, there is a famous experiment in which participants held a pen in their mouth so as to mimic either smiling or not smiling. They then saw several cartoons and rated how funny they were. What the researchers found was quite striking.
questions.prompt: What were participants asked to mimic in the pen experiment?
questions.promptZh: 持笔实验要求参与者模仿什么？
options: Either smiling or not smiling, using a pen held in the mouth.
How the characters in the cartoons moved their mouths.
The happy mood that most Americans were assumed to have.
A smile drawn on the pen before it was held in the mouth.
optionsZh: 把笔含在嘴里，模仿微笑或不微笑。
漫画人物嘴部活动的方式。
假定多数美国人具有的快乐心情。
把笔含进嘴前先模仿画在笔上的笑脸。
analyses: A so as to mimic either smiling or not smiling 明确模仿的表情与含笔操作。
B 漫画供随后评价好笑程度，文中没有模仿漫画人物嘴部动作的要求。
C 首句尚不能确定多数美国人的信念，更没有要求模仿他们的心情。
D 原句只有含笔形成表情，没有在笔上画笑脸或照着图画模仿的步骤。

vocabulary.context: 用持笔方式模拟微笑或不微笑的面部状态，不等于要求真实心情已改变。
vocabulary.example: The student tried to mimic the rhythm of the speaker's voice.

questions.translation: 我们并不能确定，多数美国人是否认为假装幸福就会使自己幸福。即便如此，有一个著名实验，让参与者嘴里叼着笔，以模拟微笑或不微笑。随后，他们观看几幅漫画，并评价其好笑程度。研究者的发现相当惊人。

evidence.quote: Even so, there is a famous experiment in which participants held a pen in their mouth so as to mimic either smiling or not smiling.

questions.editorialStatus: 逐题作者稿；已核对实际PDF原页；定位到此前未直接配题的候选句，不改写原句、不把上下文当作直接证据。

questions.passage: Those in the “smile” condition rated the same cartoons as funnier than those in the non-smile condition! Just moving their facial muscles to look like a smiley face made them enjoy the cartoons more.
questions.prompt: Which result is reported for the pen experiment in this excerpt?
options: The smile group received different and objectively funnier cartoons.
The non-smile group rated the same cartoons as funnier.
The smile group rated the same cartoons as funnier than the non-smile group.
The experiment compared naturally extraverted and introverted people.
questions.promptZh: 此片段报告叼笔实验的哪个结果？
optionsZh: 微笑组看了不同且客观更好笑的漫画。
不微笑组认为同样的漫画更好笑。
微笑组比不微笑组认为同样的漫画更好笑。
实验比较天生外向者和内向者。
analyses: A same cartoons 排除了材料不同的解释。
B 把两组评分方向倒置了。
C 正确保留组别、同样材料及比较方向；这是此处报告的实验结果。
D 分组根据表情条件，不是天生性格类型。

evidence.quote: Those in the “smile” condition rated the same cartoons as funnier than those in the non-smile condition!

vocabulary.context: 这里指微笑条件，不是疾病或身体状况
vocabulary.example: Participants were assigned to a quiet condition or a noisy condition.

questions.translation: 处于“微笑”条件的参与者对同样漫画的好笑程度评分，高于处于不微笑条件的参与者！仅仅活动面部肌肉，做出笑脸的样子，就让他们更喜欢这些漫画。
questions.editorialStatus: PDF 第 18–25 页具体原文逐题编写并视觉核对；保留限定、统计年份、观点归属及类比性质；固定无重复短段

questions.passage: Those in the “smile” condition rated the same cartoons as funnier than those in the non-smile condition! Just moving their facial muscles to look like a smiley face made them enjoy the cartoons more.
questions.prompt: What effect of the facial movement is reported in the cartoon experiment?
questions.promptZh: 漫画实验报告这种面部运动产生了什么效果？
options: It established a permanent cure for every form of sadness.
It made participants enjoy the cartoons more in that experiment.
It proved all attempts at replication would succeed.
It changed the content of the cartoons shown to each group.
optionsZh: 它确立了治愈所有悲伤的永久办法。
它使该实验中的参与者更享受漫画。
它证明所有重复实验都会成功。
它改变了每组观看的漫画内容。
analyses: A 结果针对看漫画的感受，不是任何悲伤的永久疗法。
B made them enjoy the cartoons more 是本句报告的实验内效果。
C 这两句报告的是本实验中的漫画体验，没有承诺后续每次复现都会成功。
D 句子描述面部动作，不是更换漫画；前句还明确 same cartoons。

vocabulary.context: 指用来形成类似笑脸的面部运动，不能直接替代为整个人生幸福。
vocabulary.example: The actor relaxed his facial muscles before the next scene.

questions.translation: 处于“微笑”条件的参与者对同样漫画的好笑程度评分，高于处于不微笑条件的参与者！仅仅活动面部肌肉，做出笑脸的样子，就让他们更喜欢这些漫画。

evidence.quote: Just moving their facial muscles to look like a smiley face made them enjoy the cartoons more.

questions.editorialStatus: 逐题作者稿；已核对实际PDF原页；定位到此前未直接配题的候选句，不改写原句、不把上下文当作直接证据。

questions.passage: Some failed to replicate the original findings, though others were able to replicate them. Nonetheless, the original experiment has been mentioned in major news outlets. As a result, many believe that when you are sad, you should put on a happy face.
questions.prompt: What does this passage report about attempts to replicate the original findings?
options: All attempts confirmed it without exception.
Some attempts failed to replicate it, while others succeeded.
The author says replication is irrelevant to interpretation.
No researchers ever tried to repeat it.
analyses: A all / without exception 与 Some failed 冲突。
B 同时保留失败和成功复现。
C 段落提及复现限制，未说不相关。
D 明确有重复研究。

evidence.quote: Some failed to replicate the original findings, though others were able to replicate them.

vocabulary.context: 模仿微笑的实验结果未获所有研究一致复现
vocabulary.example: Another team tried to replicate the experiment.

questions.editorialStatus: 短段版 v2；连续原句，配题片段互不重叠；保留 v1 历史快照，不重算旧成绩
questions.translation: 一些人未能复现原始发现，另一些人则成功了。尽管如此，主流新闻媒体一直提到最初的实验。结果，许多人相信，悲伤时就应该摆出一张快乐的脸。
questions.promptZh: 本段如何描述复现原始发现的尝试？
optionsZh: 所有尝试都毫无例外地确认了结果。
一些尝试未能复现，另一些则成功了。
作者说复现与解释无关。
从未有研究者尝试重复该实验。

questions.passage: There have also been many experiments in which participants were asked to behave like extraverts. Afterward, they reported more happiness than those who were asked to behave normally. Surprisingly, the intervention worked even for natural introverts. Similarly, when people were asked to talk to a stranger (i.e., acting like an extravert), people felt far happier than they had anticipated.
questions.prompt: Which statement best preserves the reported result of the extraversion experiments?
options: Only people who were already extraverts reported greater happiness.
The studies established that fake smiling works as reliably as social interaction.
Acting more extravertedly increased reported happiness, even among natural introverts.
Talking to strangers produced the amount of happiness participants had expected.
analyses: A only 排除了原文明示的 natural introverts。
B 当前片段报告外向行为及与陌生人交谈，没有比较假笑与社交互动的可靠性。
C 保留行为干预、报告结果及内向者也受益三个信息。
D 原文是 far happier than they had anticipated，不是符合原先预期。

evidence.quote: Afterward, they reported more happiness than those who were asked to behave normally.
Surprisingly, the intervention worked even for natural introverts.

vocabulary.context: 实验要求参与者表现得外向这一操作
vocabulary.example: The intervention involved a short conversation.

vocabulary.context: 与陌生人交谈后的幸福感超过事前预计
vocabulary.example: The journey took longer than we had anticipated.

questions.editorialStatus: 短段版 v2；连续原句，配题片段互不重叠；保留 v1 历史快照，不重算旧成绩
questions.translation: 还有许多实验要求参与者表现得像外向者。事后，他们报告的幸福感比被要求正常表现的人更高。令人惊讶的是，这种干预甚至对天性内向者也有效。同样，当人们被要求与陌生人交谈，也就是表现得像外向者时，他们感到的幸福远远超过自己事先的预期。
questions.promptZh: 哪一项最准确地保留了外向行为实验所报告的结果？
optionsZh: 只有原本外向的人报告幸福感增加。
研究确立假笑与社交互动同样可靠有效。
表现得更外向增加了报告的幸福感，天性内向者也如此。
与陌生人交谈产生的幸福感恰好符合参与者预期。

questions.passage: These findings have been replicated. So, acting like an extravert does tend to make people happier, even if fake smiling does not.
questions.prompt: Which statement preserves the qualification in the passage’s conclusion?
options: Acting more extraverted tends to increase happiness, even if fake smiling does not.
Fake smiling and acting extraverted always have identical effects.
Every introvert becomes permanently happier after one social interaction.
Replicated findings show that all attempts to change behaviour fail.
questions.promptZh: 哪一说法保留了本段结论的限定？
optionsZh: 表现得更外向通常会提升幸福，即使假笑没有这种作用。
假笑与外向行为总有完全相同的效果。
每个内向者只社交一次就永久更幸福。
重复验证证明所有改变行为的尝试都会失败。
analyses: A tend to 保留倾向性，even if 保留与假笑的区分。
B even if...does not 不支持效果完全相同。
C every、permanently、one 都超出原句。
D 本段对外向行为给出正向倾向，不是所有尝试失败。

evidence.quote: So, acting like an extravert does tend to make people happier, even if fake smiling does not.

vocabulary.meaning: 被重复验证；被重复研究得到
vocabulary.context: 描述研究发现的再现，不等于每位个体都有同一效果
vocabulary.example: The finding was replicated in a second study.

questions.translation: 这些发现已在后续研究中得到复现。因此，即使假笑没有这种效果，表现得像个外向者也确实往往能让人更幸福。
questions.editorialStatus: PDF 第 18–25 页具体原文逐题编写并视觉核对；保留限定、统计年份、观点归属及类比性质；固定无重复短段

questions.passage: These findings have been replicated. So, acting like an extravert does tend to make people happier, even if fake smiling does not.
questions.prompt: What does saying that findings 'have been replicated' indicate?
questions.promptZh: 说研究发现 have been replicated 表示什么？
options: The findings were reproduced in further research.
The original report was merely mentioned in a newspaper.
Every future study must produce identical results.
The authors decided not to conduct any more research.
optionsZh: 后续研究再现了这些发现。
原报告只是被报纸提到。
未来每项研究都必须有相同结果。
作者决定不再开展研究。
analyses: A replicated 指在进一步研究中再现结果；这是本句对这些发现的描述。
B 新闻提及不是科学复现，不能混淆。
C 已有复现不等于保证每个未来研究都相同。
D 当前句没有说研究者停止研究；have been replicated 表示已有复现，不是停止开展后续研究的决定。

vocabulary.meaning: 被复现；经重复研究再现
vocabulary.context: 描述研究结果在进一步研究中再现，不只是媒体转述。
vocabulary.example: The pattern was replicated in a second sample.

questions.translation: 这些发现已在后续研究中得到复现。因此，即使假笑没有这种效果，表现得像个外向者也确实往往能让人更幸福。

evidence.quote: These findings have been replicated.

questions.editorialStatus: 逐题作者稿；已核对实际PDF原页；定位到此前未直接配题的候选句，不改写原句、不把上下文当作直接证据。

questions.passage: The anagrams were impossible to solve, and everyone failed. The participants who were pressured to be happy ruminated about the failure more than the participants in the control condition, where there was no pressure to be happy.
questions.prompt: Why is the impossible-anagram experiment discussed?
options: To establish that the control group solved all the anagrams.
To recommend failure as the only route to happiness.
To prove that everyone lacks language ability.
To show that pressure to be happy can worsen reactions to the same failure.
analyses: A control 组也失败，并未解开所有字谜。
B 实验关注压力和反应，不是建议追求失败。
C impossible 的任务设计不能推断所有人语言能力不足。
D everyone failed 表明两组都未解出题；承受快乐压力的一组却更多地反复琢磨失败，支持压力可能使反应更糟。

evidence.quote: The anagrams were impossible to solve, and everyone failed.
The participants who were pressured to be happy ruminated about the failure more than the participants in the control condition, where there was no pressure to be happy.

vocabulary.context: 反复想着解不开字谜的失败
vocabulary.example: He ruminated about the meeting for hours.

questions.editorialStatus: 短段版 v2；连续原句，配题片段互不重叠；保留 v1 历史快照，不重算旧成绩
questions.translation: 这些字谜根本无法解开，所有人都失败了。被施加快乐压力的参与者，比没有这种压力的对照组参与者更反复地琢磨这次失败。
questions.promptZh: 为什么讨论无法解开的字谜实验？
optionsZh: 证明对照组解出了全部字谜。
建议把失败作为幸福的唯一路径。
证明所有人都缺乏语言能力。
说明必须快乐的压力可能使人对同样的失败反应更糟。

questions.passage: Interestingly, in the countries where happiness is more strongly associated with good luck and fortune than personal accomplishments (e.g., Japan and Germany), there appears to be less pressure to be happy.
questions.prompt: Which conclusion stays within the evidence of the international comparison?
options: Every American feels more pressure than every Japanese person.
Countries associating happiness more with luck appeared to show less pressure to be happy.
Cultural associations were experimentally assigned to entire nations.
Belief in luck has been proved to remove all sadness.
analyses: A 原句谈国家层面的文化联系与压力，没有给出每个美国人都比每个日本人压力大的个体排序。
B 保留 countries、association 和 appeared 的谨慎程度。
C 片段没有国家层面的随机分配。
D remove all sadness 与相关比较完全不同。

evidence.quote: Interestingly, in the countries where happiness is more strongly associated with good luck and fortune than personal accomplishments (e.g., Japan and Germany), there appears to be less pressure to be happy.

vocabulary.context: 幸福与好运或成就的文化联系
vocabulary.example: This colour is often associated with spring.

questions.editorialStatus: 短段版 v2；连续原句，配题片段互不重叠；保留 v1 历史快照，不重算旧成绩

Perhaps there could be more to life than coziness and small joys, at least once in a while. Happiness is not the only way to lead a good life, as we shall see.
questions.prompt: What does the author ask the reader to do after acknowledging existing happiness?
questions.promptZh: 肯定已有的幸福之后，作者请读者做什么？
options: Assume that contentment is the only possible good life.
Reject all ordinary decisions made in the past.
Prove that every maximizer is unhappy.
Pause to reflect on the satisficer mindset.
optionsZh: 认定知足是唯一可能的好生活。
拒绝过去所有普通决定。
证明每个最优追求者都不幸福。
停下来反思满意即可的心态。
analyses: A 本段结尾说幸福不是唯一方式，不能改成唯一。
B reflect 不等于拒绝所有旧决定。
C 没有要求证明每个 maximizer 的情绪。
D But take a moment to reflect... 明示邀请审视心态，并非要求永久放弃它。

vocabulary.context: 邀请读者审视 satisficer mindset 的局限，而非一概否定知足。
vocabulary.example: She took time to reflect on what she wanted from the next year.

questions.translation: 如果你感到必须时时快乐的压力，请记住：偶尔悲伤、愤怒或害怕是可以的。这些情绪会为你的内心生活增添复杂性与丰富性。如果你已经对自己的人生感到幸福，你也做得很好。不过，花一点时间反思一下自己“满意即可”的选择心态。至少偶尔，人生或许还可以不止于温馨舒适和小小乐趣。正如我们接下来会看到的，幸福不是过上美好生活的唯一方式。

evidence.quote: But take a moment to reflect on your satisficer mindset.

questions.passage: Happiness has many fans. But, there are also many doubters, ranging from the Stoics to Gustave Flaubert. Flaubert wrote to Louise Colet, “To be stupid, selfish, and have good health are three requirements for happiness, though if stupidity is lacking, all is lost.” In a similar spirit, Tony Schwartz wrote an article entitled “Happiness Is Overrated” in the Harvard Business Review, saying, “ ‘Happy’ people are some of the dullest people I know.”
questions.prompt: How is Flaubert's remark about requirements for happiness presented?
questions.promptZh: 福楼拜关于幸福条件的说法以什么方式呈现？
options: As the narrator's own final definition of happiness.
As a neutral summary of the Stoics’ definition of happiness.
As a sceptical view expressed in a letter to Louise Colet.
As a diagnostic rule established by a medical survey.
optionsZh: 作为叙述者自己的最终幸福定义。
作为对斯多葛学派幸福定义的中立总结。
作为写给路易丝·科莱信中的怀疑看法。
作为医学调查确立的诊断规则。
analyses: A Flaubert wrote to 明确另一个说话来源，不能移给叙述者。
B Flaubert wrote to Louise Colet 标明福楼拜书信中的看法，不是把它归为斯多葛学派的中立定义。
C 句子给出作者和收信人，语境列举幸福的怀疑者，应按书信观点理解。
D 尖锐引语不等于经验证的诊断标准，也不能据此给所有幸福者贴标签。

vocabulary.context: 是福楼拜书信中的尖锐说法，不是本书建立的医学条件。
vocabulary.example: The guide lists the basic requirements for submitting an application.

questions.translation: 幸福有许多拥护者。但也有许多怀疑者，从斯多葛学派到 Gustave Flaubert 都在其中。Flaubert 写信给 Louise Colet 说：“愚蠢、自私和身体健康，是幸福的三个条件；不过，如果缺少愚蠢，一切就都完了。”Tony Schwartz 也抱着类似态度，在《哈佛商业评论》发表题为《幸福被高估了》的文章，说：“‘幸福’的人是我认识的人中最乏味的一些。”

evidence.quote: Flaubert wrote to Louise Colet, “To be stupid, selfish, and have good health are three requirements for happiness, though if stupidity is lacking, all is lost.”

questions.passage: Why so down on happiness? One common critique is that a happy life might be a selfish one. In reality, there is lots of evidence that suggests otherwise. For example, spending money on others as opposed to on oneself increases happiness.
questions.prompt: What does being 'down on happiness' mean in the rhetorical question?
questions.promptZh: 反问中 down on happiness 是什么意思？
options: Believing that happiness has become less common over time.
Feeling sad because one cannot attain happiness.
Ranking happiness below every other goal in life.
Being critical or disapproving of happiness.
optionsZh: 认为幸福随时间推移变得较少见。
因为无法获得幸福而感到难过。
把幸福排在生活其他所有目标之下。
对幸福持批评或不赞同态度。
analyses: A down on 表示态度，当前问句没有报告幸福随时间变少的趋势。
B 这里问对幸福这一观念的批评态度，不等于因为自己无法幸福而难过。
C 段落提出一种 common critique，没有给出幸福低于其他每一种目标的完整排序。
D 紧接着的 One common critique 展开批评理由，支持此处不赞同、批评的短语义。

vocabulary.context: 问为什么对幸福如此批评，不是说某个读者情绪低落。
vocabulary.example: The reviewer was down on the plan because it ignored local needs.

questions.translation: 为什么如此贬低幸福？一种常见批评认为，幸福的生活可能是自私的生活。实际上，有大量证据指向相反的情况。例如，把钱花在别人身上而不是自己身上，会增加幸福感。

evidence.quote: Why so down on happiness?

questions.passage: The novelist Donna Tartt suggested that it is “to make other people happy even at the expense of one’s own happiness”—in other words, what many scholars call a “meaningful life.” Meaning in life is typically defined by significance, purpose, and coherence. First, a meaningful life is a life that matters. It matters not just to one’s family members and friends, but also to strangers.
questions.prompt: What does 'at the expense of one’s own happiness' mean in Tartt's suggestion?
questions.promptZh: 塔特建议中的 at the expense of one's own happiness 是什么意思？
options: Calculating a financial fee for every helpful action.
Making others happy even if this sacrifices one's own happiness.
Helping only when one's own happiness is guaranteed to increase.
Treating others' happiness as less important in every circumstance.
optionsZh: 为每次助人计算经济收费。
即便牺牲自己的幸福，也让别人幸福。
只有保证自己幸福增加时才帮助。
任何情况下都把别人幸福视为更不重要。
analyses: A expense 是以……为代价的短语义，并非收费。
B even at the expense of 明确容许自己的幸福付出代价；这是小说家提出的看法。
C even if sacrifice 与 only when guaranteed gain 相反。
D 该建议重视别人幸福，不是总把别人放低。不能把引述的价值看法当作唯一合法生活方式或实验结论。

vocabulary.context: 指让自己幸福受损的可能代价，而非金钱支出。
vocabulary.example: The team sought speed, but not at the expense of accuracy.
collocations: at the expense of one’s happiness

questions.translation: 小说家 Donna Tartt 提出，美好生活就是“让别人幸福，即使以牺牲自己的幸福为代价”——换言之，许多学者所说的“有意义的生活”。生命意义通常由重要性、目的和连贯性来界定。首先，有意义的生活是有分量的生活。它不仅对自己的家人朋友有分量，对陌生人也如此。

questions.passage: In contrast, a meaningless life is a life that does not make any difference in the world. Anthropologist David Graeber, in his book Bullshit Jobs: A Theory, argues that there are millions of people around the world who are toiling away their lives in meaningless jobs. He defines a bullshit job as a job that the person who is doing it can’t really justify the existence of that job.
questions.prompt: What contrast is introduced in the description of a meaningless life?
questions.promptZh: 描述无意义人生时，引入了什么对照？
options: Fame is contrasted with a high income.
One occupation is declared more prestigious than every other.
Making a difference is contrasted with making no difference in the world.
All repetitive work is contrasted with all meaningful relationships.
optionsZh: 名声与高收入的对照。
宣布某一职业比其他所有职业更有声望。
在世界上产生影响与没有产生影响的对照。
所有重复工作与所有有意义关系的对照。
analyses: A In contrast 在这里不是比较收入和名声。
B 没有职业声望排名。
C does not make any difference 用否定结构描述无意义人生，形成“产生影响／没有产生影响”的对照。
D 这一句没有把工作与关系分成两组，也不能由后面职业例子推断所有重复工作无意义。

vocabulary.context: 把意义的影响维度与其缺失相对照，不是另立职业优劣榜。
vocabulary.example: The first route is busy; in contrast, the second is usually quiet.

questions.translation: 相比之下，无意义的生活是对世界不产生任何影响的生活。人类学家 David Graeber 在《毫无意义的工作：一种理论》中认为，世界各地有数百万人正辛苦地把生命耗费在无意义的工作上。他把这种工作定义为：连从事它的人自己都无法真正说明其存在理由的工作。

evidence.quote: In contrast, a meaningless life is a life that does not make any difference in the world.

questions.passage: Meaningless jobs, according to Graeber, are not just repetitive factory or clerical jobs, but also include corporate lawyers, public relations consultants, telemarketers, and brand managers. For instance, he claims that most corporate lawyers secretly believe that the world would probably be a better place if they did not exist. questions.prompt: Why does the author say these occupations do not necessarily imply meaningless lives?
options: People can make a difference outside their jobs.
Graeber excludes all professional occupations from his argument.
The author claims that every corporate lawyer secretly enjoys the work.
A job’s repetitiveness guarantees a meaningful life.

工作的重复性保证人生有意义。
analyses: A outside of their jobs 是最后结论的直接理由。
B 列出的 corporate lawyers 等恰恰属于论述范围。
C 原文归于 Graeber 的说法涉及职业存在，不是所有人喜欢工作。
D 重复性不是人生有意义的保证。

evidence.quote: Of course, people can make a difference in the world outside of their jobs. So this doesn’t mean corporate lawyers and public relations consultants lead meaningless lives.

questions.passage: Psychologist Michael Steger and colleagues asked participants to report how meaningful they feel their lives are. In addition, he asked their friends and family members to report the participant’s meaning in life. If the high percentage of self-reported meaning in life is only an illusion, informant reports would not correlate with self-reports. What he found was different: self-reported meaning in life is correlated with informant-reported meaning in life.

How meaningful they felt their own lives were.

亲友的评分是否已经与本人一致。

Religious people follow certain principles of faith, which help them interpret difficult life situations accordingly and give them clarity. options: They struggled to choose a shared religious principle.
They struggled to understand why the catastrophe had happened.
They had no difficulty making sense of the catastrophe.
They could not understand the survey’s percentage calculation.
