questions.passage: Steger’s research also finds that people who say they have a meaningful life tend to be optimistic about the future, extraverted, non-neurotic, agreeable, conscientious, and have high self-esteem. Only scientists can assess whether their lives have meaning.
Ordinary people lack any connection to a significant mission.
Subjective meaning does not necessarily follow external success or status.

主观意义感不必然随外在成就或地位而来。

In contrast, some ordinary people see their lives as linked to a significant mission.

questions.passage: Second, people with high self-esteem are more likely to say that their lives matter than those who do not like themselves. Non-neurotic people (those who don’t worry too much or are not too stress prone) are more likely to say that their lives have a clear purpose and direction than neurotic people. Everyone who dislikes themselves has independently proved that their life does not matter.

自尊被说成与任何自报无关。

B more likely 明示一种联系，不是完全无关。

questions.passage: Hesse is not the only author to suggest the importance of exploration. As with Narcissus and Goldmund, at the core of Søren Kierkegaard’s Either/Or is this dilemma: Should we pursue an aesthetic life or a virtuous life? A promotes an aesthetic life, or the life of beauty and adventure.

Whether Author A and Author B have confirmed historical identities.
Whether Hesse and Kierkegaard used the same literary form.
Whether to pursue an aesthetic life or a virtuous life.
optionsZh: 美与冒险是否等同于德性。
Author A 与 Author B 的历史身份是否已经确认。
Hesse 与 Kierkegaard 是否采用相同的文学形式。
应该追求审美生活，还是有德的生活。
analyses: A 原文提出两种生活之间的追求选择，没有把两者是否相等写成核心两难。
B presumably 限定人物身份的推测程度，但核心问题是怎样生活，不是核实履历。
C As with 引出相似主题，不等于把两位作者的文学形式是否一致设为核心两难。
D at the core...this dilemma 后直接给出 Should we pursue an aesthetic life or a virtuous life，选项保留选择对象和方向。

questions.passage: Again and again, what these novels focus on is a fascination with and admiration of a life of exploration. Stephen Dedalus in James Joyce’s A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man also chooses the life of aesthetics over virtue. questions.promptZh: 文中把什么选择归于斯蒂芬·迪达勒斯？
options: He chooses security over every form of artistic experience.
He rejects both aesthetics and virtue as irrelevant.
He chooses the same monastic office as Narcissus.
He chooses a life of aesthetics over virtue.
optionsZh: 他选择安全而放弃任何艺术体验。
他认为审美和德性都无关而拒绝两者。

questions.passage: In a 2015 Atlantic essay, Alison Gopnik, a world-famous professor of psychology at UC Berkeley, wrote, “In 2006, I was 50—I was falling apart.” When her children left for college, her long marriage to her husband unraveled. questions.prompt: Which sequence of events does Gopnik describe?
options: She left for college, moved into a larger house, and then married.
Her marriage ended after she accepted a new position at Berkeley.
She stayed in the family home when her children left for college.
Her children left for college, her marriage unravelled, and she moved to live alone.
questions.promptZh: Gopnik 描述的哪组事件顺序正确？
optionsZh: 她上大学、搬进更大的房子，然后结婚。
她在接受 Berkeley 新职位后婚姻结束。
孩子上大学时，她继续住在原家庭住宅。
孩子上大学、婚姻破裂，她搬出独居。
analyses: A 上大学的是孩子，不是当时五十岁的她；住所也并非更大。
B Berkeley 在这里是教授身份信息；片段没有说她接受新职位，也没有给出新任职与婚姻瓦解的先后关系。
C moved out of...home 明确搬离。
D 保留孩子离家、婚姻瓦解与搬出独居的叙述顺序，不另造因果。

questions.passage: What about a psychologically rich day? Mary Oliver in her poem “Wild Geese” tells us that we don’t have to be extraordinarily good or virtuous, that despair is a part of life, and that insignificance is a part of existence. Even so, she encourages us to be like wild geese: “the world offers itself to your imagination.” The world has so much to offer and explore: “harsh and exciting.”
questions.prompt: Which dimension does the question 'What about a psychologically rich day' bring into focus?
questions.promptZh: What about a psychologically rich day 把哪个维度带入焦点？
options: Only daily pleasure.
Only moral goodness.
Financial wealth.
Psychological richness.
optionsZh: 只有日常愉悦。
只有道德善良。
财务财富。
心理丰富性。
analyses: A 不是继续只问开心，psychologically rich 有明确不同名称。
B 后文诗歌还说不必格外有德，不能把道德完美设为唯一维度。
C psychologically 排除了财务 rich 的偷换。
D 问句明确提出 psychologically rich day，并以 Oliver 的诗讨论这一维度。

vocabulary.meaning: 那么……呢；把相关话题引向另一对象
vocabulary.context: 当前将关注点引向心理丰富的一天，是相关话题的追问，而非已经得到的数值答案。

Extraordinary virtue is not a prerequisite, and despair and insignificance are acknowledged as parts of life.
The poem proves that every harmful action benefits others.
The poem declares every person's existence wholly worthless.

C 不要求道德完美不是鼓励伤害，更不是实验因果结论。

questions.passage: In addition to asking about happiness, meaning, and psychological richness, we asked them how typical or atypical each day was, how many routine activities they participated in, how much free time they had, and whether they did something new, met someone new, or ate something new. We also presented them with an activity checklist that asked them whether they volunteered, went to a concert, hiked, played a video game, and so on. These daily reports gave us a nice picture of how the students spent their days.
questions.prompt: What did the activity checklist ask about?
options: Only students’ grades and family income.
The researcher’s judgement of which activity students should choose.
Whether students had volunteered, attended concerts, hiked, played video games, and similar activities.
Only whether the day had been happy, with no questions about behaviour.

optionsZh: 只问成绩与家庭收入。
研究者判断学生应该选哪项活动。
是否志愿服务、听音乐会、徒步、玩电子游戏等。
只问当天是否幸福，完全不问行为。
analyses: A 这些项目没有出现在本段清单。
B asked whether 是询问已做的事，不是分配应做的事。
C 对应清单明确列出的活动例子。
D In addition to 说明除感受外还问常规、新事物和具体活动。

evidence.quote: an activity checklist that asked them whether they volunteered, went to a concert, hiked, played a video game, and so on.

vocabulary.context: 在研究中列出活动供参与者报告，不是活动指令

questions.passage: First, we found some common factors associated with all three aspects of well-being. It turned out that doing something new, eating something new, or meeting someone new enhanced not only psychological richness but also happiness and meaning. That is, most students reported that their day was happier, more meaningful, and richer on a day when they did something new, ate something new, or met someone new.
questions.prompt: Which conclusion stays closest to the reported finding?
options: Every person becomes happier whenever they try any new food.
Novelty affected psychological richness but never meaning or happiness.
The study randomly assigned novelty and established a universal causal law.
Most students reported all three qualities more positively on days involving something new.
questions.promptZh: 哪项结论最贴近报告的发现？
optionsZh: 每个人每次尝试任何新食物都更幸福。
新奇只影响心理丰富，绝不涉及意义或幸福。
研究随机分配新奇经历，确立普遍因果规律。
多数学生在包含新事物的日子，对三个维度都报告得更积极。
analyses: A most students 与 every person、whenever 的范围不同。
B not only...but also 明确涉及三个维度。
C 片段说 associated 和 reported，没有随机操控的说明。
D 保留多数、日子比较和自报性质，不额外保证因果。

evidence.quote: most students reported that their day was happier, more meaningful, and richer on a day when they did something new, ate something new, or met someone new.

vocabulary.context: 指观察到的共同变化，不能自动读成随机试验确证因果

questions.translation: 首先，我们发现一些与幸福、意义和心理丰富这三个方面都相关的共同因素。结果显示，在做新事、吃新食物或遇见新人的日子里，心理丰富感、幸福感与意义感都更高。也就是说，多数学生报告，自己做新事、吃新食物或遇见新人的那一天更幸福、更有意义，心理体验也更丰富。

questions.passage: Second, we found some unique predictors of a psychologically rich day. For instance, an atypical day was psychologically richer than a typical day, but an atypical day was not happier than a typical day. A day with more free time was psychologically richer than a day with less free time. In contrast, a free day was no more meaningful than a less free day.
questions.prompt: What does the second group of findings introduce?
questions.promptZh: 第二组发现引入什么？
options: Only the same factors shared by every dimension.
The financial costs of each diary entry.
Predictors that distinguish psychological richness from the other dimensions.
A proof that all happiness and meaning scores were zero.
optionsZh: 只有每个维度完全共享的同一因素。
每篇日记的经济成本。
使心理丰富与其他维度区分开的预测因素。
证明所有幸福和意义分数为零。

B 没有日记成本问题。
C 后例 atypical 更丰富却不更幸福、空闲更丰富却不更有意义，说明区分性预测。
D 不是说其他维度全为零，差异比较不可当成不存在。predictor 也不自动等于因果。

questions.passage: Finally, a day with more required work was happier and more meaningful than a day with less required work. That is, getting things done made the day happier and more meaningful, whereas doing something unusual made the day psychologically richer. Whether you’re taking a short trip to a vineyard, walking in an unfamiliar part of town, going to a baseball game, or calling an old friend from elementary school, doing something that you don’t usually do is more interesting and psychologically rich than doing things you do every day.
questions.prompt: Which dimensions were higher on days with more required work in the reported comparison?
questions.promptZh: 报告的比较中，必须完成任务更多的日子哪些维度更高？
options: Psychological richness alone.
Happiness and meaning.
Financial wealth alone.
None of the dimensions was compared.
optionsZh: 只有心理丰富。
幸福与意义。
只有财务财富。
没有比较任何维度。
analyses: A 目标句写 happier and more meaningful，不是 richness alone。
B 两个比较形容词明确对应幸福和意义。
C 没有收入或财产测量。
D more...than 明确进行比较。按日记研究报告理解这一模式，不升级为过量工作对所有人的必然益处。

vocabulary.meaning: 必须完成的任务；需要做的工作
vocabulary.context: 不是所有自愿探索，也不能自动等同全职职业或法律强制。

questions.translation: 最后，必须完成的工作更多的一天，比这类工作较少的一天更幸福、更有意义。也就是说，完成事务的日子更幸福、更有意义，而做不寻常事情的日子心理上更丰富。无论短途去葡萄园、走进城里陌生街区、看棒球赛，还是给小学老友打电话，做平时不常做的事，都比每天重复的事更有趣、更具心理丰富性。

evidence.quote: Finally, a day with more required work was happier and more meaningful than a day with less required work.

questions.passage: In her popular book Bittersweet, Susan Cain contends that “light and dark, birth and death—bitter and sweet—are forever paired” and that negative emotions such as sorrow and longing “make us whole.” She argues that negative emotions play a central role in our emotional lives and make us more empathetic and even more creative. Similarly, I think that negative emotions such as sorrow and longing, along with positive emotions, make our lives psychologically richer.
questions.prompt: How does the author position his view alongside Susan Cain’s?
options: Both accounts give negative emotions a role, and the author links their combination with positive emotions to richness.
The author rejects Cain because he thinks only positive feelings matter.
Cain is described as having conducted the author’s final experiment.
Both claim that negative emotions guarantee happiness in every person.
questions.promptZh: 作者怎样把自己的观点与 Susan Cain 的观点联系起来？
optionsZh: 两者都赋予负面情绪作用，作者把正负情绪的组合与丰富性相连。
作者认为只有正面情绪重要，所以否定 Cain。
Cain 被说成开展了作者最后的实验。
两者都断言负面情绪保证所有人幸福。
analyses: A Similarly 引出与 Cain 相似的重视，同时明确 along with positive emotions。
B Similarly 是相呼应，并非否定或只保留正面。
C 本段引书与观点，没有实验执行者说明。
D richer 不是幸福保证，且 I think 和 argues 均标明观点归属。

evidence.quote: Similarly, I think that negative emotions such as sorrow and longing, along with positive emotions, make our lives psychologically richer.

To guarantee that all remaining words were equally familiar to everyone.

To seek relatively neutral vocabulary and reduce bias in personality research.

questions.passage: But why rely on words to illuminate an inner quality? Allport and Odbert argued, “If many human beings were not in fact egotistic, aggressive, or timid, the epithets would not have found a permanent place in language. People becoming different because of dictionary labels.
Every speaker learning exactly the same vocabulary.

optionsZh: 研究者发现每个称谓都代表一种独立特质。

sourceSegments.text: For example, Lew Goldberg had 187 college students rate themselves on 1,710 terms: “How jolly are you in general? How reserved are you in general? How sadistic are you in general?” and so on.

questions.passage: Goldberg’s study and others like it found that many personality traits cluster neatly into the following five factors: extraversion (e.g., jolly, talkative, sociable, active), neuroticism (e.g., touchy, fearful, self-critical), conscientiousness (e.g., persistent, tidy, dependable), agreeableness (e.g., generous, kind, trustful), and openness to experience (e.g., literary, insightful, perceptive). In a sense, personality psychologists created a map. Like cities and towns across the world, there are countless words descriptive of personality. By classifying all these words into five factors, personality psychologists essentially organized them into “continents” on the map.
questions.prompt: What does the comparison with continents help explain?
options: Many personality-describing words are organised into a few broad factors.
Each personality trait belongs to a particular geographical continent.
The five factors correspond to five named countries.
Psychologists count only traits associated with large cities.
questions.promptZh: 把人格因子比作大陆，有助于说明什么？
optionsZh: 大量人格描述词被整理为少数宽泛因子。
每种人格特质都属于某个地理大陆。
五个因子分别对应五个具名国家。
心理学家只统计与大城市有关的特质。
analyses: A words 对应城镇，five factors 对应大陆，突出归类层级。
B 比喻不能改成真实地理归属。
C 原文五因子是外向、神经质、尽责、宜人和经验开放性，没有五国配对。
D countless words 表示广泛词汇，并非只筛城市有关的特质。

evidence.quote: By classifying all these words into five factors, personality psychologists essentially organized them into “continents” on the map.

vocabulary.context: 人格描述词按关联形成较大的组，并非地理迁移
vocabulary.example: The responses cluster around three broad themes.

questions.translation: Goldberg 的研究及类似研究发现，许多人格特质可以整齐归入五个因子：外向性（如快活、健谈、合群、活跃），神经质（如敏感易恼、容易害怕、自我批评），尽责性（如坚持不懈、整洁、可靠），宜人性（如慷慨、友善、信任他人），以及经验开放性（如爱好文学、有洞见、感知敏锐）。从某种意义说，人格心理学家创造了一张地图。像世界各地的城镇一样，描述人格的词数不胜数。把这些词归为五个因子，就相当于把它们整理为地图上的“大陆”。

questions.passage: Why do people who are high in openness to experience tend to lead psychologically rich lives? Open people are imaginative, curious, and interested in intellectual and artistic pursuits. People low in openness are conventional and down-to-earth, preferring routine and less interested in intellectual or artistic pursuits. Students who are open to experience are more likely to study abroad, an activity known to enhance psychological richness, than those low in openness.

比低开放性学生更可能留学。
大学里全部选择同一种艺术学科。
analyses: A 原文说 open people 对知识和艺术有兴趣。
B preferring routine 修饰低开放性者。
C 最后一句明确比较留学可能性；more likely 不等于所有人。
D 没有统一选科的信息，也不能把倾向扩成全体。

evidence.quote: Students who are open to experience are more likely to study abroad, an activity known to enhance psychological richness, than those low in openness.

questions.passage: The two strongest personality predictors of a happy life are emotional stability and extraversion. Some personality scholars conceptualize extraversion as positive affectivity (good moods) and neuroticism as negative affectivity (bad moods). Since by definition a happy life is the preponderance of positive emotions and relative lack of negative emotions, it makes sense that extraversion and emotional stability are the most characteristic of a happy life.
questions.prompt: Why does the author say the two strongest predictors of happiness “make sense”?
options: Their affective meanings align with a definition emphasising positive over negative emotions.
They prove that happy people never experience negative emotion.
They show that openness is the same thing as emotional stability.
Their names demonstrate that personality never changes.
questions.promptZh: 作者为什么说幸福的两项最强预测因素“合乎道理”？

它们证明幸福者从不体验消极情绪。
它们说明开放性与情绪稳定性是同一概念。
它们的名称证明人格永不改变。
analyses: A some scholars 对外向性与神经质的概念化，和幸福的情绪定义相衔接，形成文中的理由。
B relative lack 是相对较少，不是绝对没有。
C 没有将开放性等同情绪稳定性。
D 本段讨论概念和关联，不讨论人格是否永不变化。

questions.passage: Finally, why is openness to experience uncorrelated to a happy life? One potential reason is the greater motivation to explore among open people. But when the exploration results in a negative experience, it is not.

As proof that trying a new restaurant always increases happiness.
As evidence that open people never have unpleasant experiences.

声称每次探索都必定减少幸福。

D 正面结果与更高幸福相联，不能说所有探索都减少幸福；uncorrelated 也不等于对每个人都毫无关系。

questions.passage: At age fifteen, Greta began protesting in front of the Swedish parliament every Friday with a sign that read, “School Strike for Climate.” Her movement, dubbed “Fridays for Future,” spread around the world. She catalyzed a host of youth climate activism, and to date continues to advocate for reducing carbon emissions and increasing sustainability. Greta is endlessly committed to her work.
questions.prompt: What information does 'dubbed Fridays for Future' provide?
questions.promptZh: dubbed Fridays for Future 提供什么信息？
options: The wording on the original protest sign rather than the movement's name.
The name given to the movement that spread internationally.
A name given to Huckabee's religious cause.
The only day on which people worldwide can act on climate issues.
optionsZh: 原抗议牌的文字，而不是运动名称。
传播到国际的那场运动所取名称。
Huckabee 宗教事业的名称。
全球人们唯一能行动的日期。
analyses: A 牌上是 School Strike for Climate，Fridays for Future 是运动名，不可互换。
B dubbed 表被称为，名称与运动对应。
C Her movement 对应当前的 Greta 及她的气候行动，不能错配成另一人物的宗教事业。
D 名称不建立全世界只能某天行动的规则，spread 说传播而不是所有人参加。

vocabulary.context: 给运动命名的被动分词，不是电影配音义。

questions.passage: Conscientious people are well organized, careful, and thorough. They have clear goals and pursue them diligently. It follows that, in order to pursue your goals successfully, you can’t worry too much about various barriers to success or get discouraged too easily when things don’t go well. Thus, lower levels of neuroticism (not worrying too much) are helpful.
questions.prompt: What does 'Thus' connect to the claim about lower neuroticism?
questions.promptZh: Thus 怎样连接到较低神经质有帮助的说法？
options: It draws a conclusion from the preceding discussion of excessive worry and discouragement.
It reverses the preceding argument and recommends maximal worry.
It gives a date when a clinical diagnosis was made.
It states that all anxiety makes meaning impossible.
optionsZh: 从前面过度担忧与容易灰心的讨论得出结论。
反转前文并建议最大程度忧虑。
给出临床诊断日期。
断言任何焦虑都使意义不可能。
analyses: A Thus 是结论标记，括号 not worrying too much 呼应前文。
B 是较低有帮助，不是最大忧虑。
C 无诊断或日期。
D 当前只说较低水平有帮助，too much 又限定为过度担忧；不能推出任何焦虑都排除意义。

questions.passage: So, who is likely to lead a psychologically rich life? In terms of personality traits, people who are open to experience and extraverted are most likely to lead a psychologically rich life. They are more likely to do something new, meet someone new, or learn something new, like Goldmund in Narcissus and Goldmund. These relationships are not deterministic, however.
questions.prompt: What does the opening 'So, who is likely ...?' do in the summary?

It declares a deterministic rule with no possible exceptions.

It takes up the question of who is likely to lead a rich life and gives a qualified summary.
optionsZh: 无关前文地引入新讣告样本。
宣布无例外的决定性定律。
仅问谁最有钱。
提出谁较可能过心理丰富生活的问题，并给出有限定的总结。

B likely 及末句 not deterministic 限制强度。
C rich 是心理丰富而非财富。
D 问句随后由人格特质与more likely作答，末句not deterministic保留非必然性。

questions.passage: Who is happy? Extraverts and emotionally stable people tend to lead a happy life perhaps in part because they tend to have good relationships and find something positive in most situations. Conscientious people tend to be happy as well, perhaps because they tend to achieve their goals, whereas agreeable people tend to be happy in part because they have warm, conflict-free relationships with others.
questions.prompt: How strongly are the explanations for happiness presented here?
options: As the single proven cause of every happy life.
As partial explanations, with some explicitly qualified by “perhaps”.
As evidence that agreeable people never face disagreement.
As a denial that goal achievement has any relationship with happiness.
questions.promptZh: 本段以多强的确定程度解释幸福？
optionsZh: 每种幸福人生唯一且已证实的原因。
部分解释，其中一些明确用 perhaps 限定。
证明宜人者从不遭遇任何分歧。
否认目标实现与幸福有任何联系。
analyses: A tend、perhaps、in part 均避免唯一和必然。
B 两处 perhaps 和 in part 表明这是部分、带限定的机制解释。
C warm, conflict-free relationships 是作者描述的倾向，不是每个人永无冲突。
D 作者确实把目标实现作为尽责者可能更幸福的解释之一。

perhaps because they tend to achieve their goals

questions.passage: At the core of a psychologically rich personality are openness to experience and extraversion. One might ask, though: How can those of us who don’t have those basic personality traits become more open and extraverted? One answer is to embrace playfulness. In a 1980 study, when Robert McCrae and Paul Costa asked 240 men to complete various sentences such as, “What gets me into trouble is…” and “When his wife asked him to do the housework…,” open-minded men’s responses were far more playful than closed-minded men’s responses.

questions.passage: For instance, a man high in openness to experience said, “When my wife asked me to do the housework, I invented an urgent excuse.” A closed-minded man would have responded, “When my wife asked me to do the housework, I reluctantly did.” McCrae and Costa observed, “The final distinguishing characteristic of open men is a playful, sometimes odd, sense of humor. A slight twist may be given to meanings, and obviously playful objections to the test are frequently made.”
questions.prompt: Which interpretation respects the contrasting housework responses?

questions.passage: But what exactly is being playful? The psychoanalyst Erik Erikson described it best: when you are playful, you are “on vacation from social and economic reality.” All of us adults have a lot of social and economic responsibilities. That is the reality.

questions.passage: Hinds partnered with Mark Mortensen to survey forty-nine teams in the research and development division of a single multinational corporation. The results showed that geographically distributed teams had far less spontaneous communication, less shared identity, and far more task conflict than those in geographically concentrated teams. Hinds and Mortensen concluded that “spontaneous communication contributes to a shared identity, facilitates the creation of shared context, and aids distributed teams in identifying and resolving conflicts before they escalate.”
questions.prompt: What pattern was reported for the geographically distributed teams in the survey?

analyses: A 三个比较方向都倒置。
B 结果明确报告差别。

questions.passage: To be clear, specialization and professionalism are great for skill acquisition and improvement. But remember the fate of Jack (played by Jack Nicholson) in Stanley Kubrick’s movie The Shining: all work and no play not only make Jack a dull boy, but also make him go nuts at the end. When winning becomes everything, life gets too heavy. A playful mindset can help people who are psychologically stuck move past their low points and enjoy the journey, not just the outcome.
questions.prompt: Which balance does the author advocate in this passage?
options: Reject skill development because professionalism has no value.
Value specialisation while using playfulness to enjoy the journey beyond winning alone.
Treat the fictional film as experimental proof about every professional.
Measure a life only by whether it wins every competition.

optionsZh: 专业化没有价值，因此拒绝技能发展。
肯定专攻的价值，同时用玩心享受过程，不只盯获胜。
把虚构电影当作关于所有专业人士的实验证明。
只用能否赢每次比赛衡量人生。
analyses: A 首句明确肯定技能习得与提高。
B 作者先肯定 specialization 和 professionalism 的技能价值，再指出把获胜看作一切的沉重，并提出享受过程、不只重结果的玩心。
C Jack 是 The Shining 的电影角色，不能当临床或因果实验结论。
D winning becomes everything 正是作者所质疑的状态。can help 不等于对所有心理困难的治疗保证。

questions.passage: A spontaneous action could help us experience life without prior planning. Some of the most interesting experiences we have are often things we do on a whim. In my case, I was driving my family from Baltimore to Charlottesville one day when I saw a sign for Annapolis. I asked my wife and two kids, “Does anyone want to go to Annapolis?”
questions.prompt: Which paraphrase preserves 'Some ... often ... on a whim'?
questions.promptZh: 哪项改述保留 Some...often...on a whim 的范围？
options: Every interesting event is always planned far ahead.
Some especially interesting experiences often arise from unplanned impulses.
Only careless decisions can ever produce interest.
All planned experiences are necessarily uninteresting.
optionsZh: 每件有趣事总提前很久安排。
一些特别有趣的经历往往来自临时兴起。
只有粗心决定才有可能有趣。
所有计划内经历必定无趣。
analyses: A 与on a whim对照且擅加every。
B Some和often不是全部，on a whim为临时念头。
C 自发不等于粗心，更非only条件。
D 未否定计划体验的所有乐趣；后面家庭故事为个例。

vocabulary.context: 可指有趣自发决定，不自动等于危险、粗心或完全无意识。

questions.passage: Yes, our patio project produced a lot of stress, physical pain, and unhappiness during those three months. Outsourcing would have increased happiness in the short run. In the long run, however, we now have far more stories that we can tell our friends, as well as the undiluted raw emotion of pride, a sense of accomplishment, and memories of agony and pain.
questions.prompt: How does the author distinguish short-run and long-run consequences?

Doing it themselves produced no negative feelings at the time and no later memories.
Hiring help actually gave them all the same stories while removing every cost.
The project guaranteed permanent happiness and erased memories of pain.
questions.promptZh: 作者怎样区分短期与长期后果？

analyses: A would have 是外包的反事实判断；In the long run 则转向如今真实拥有的故事、骄傲与苦痛记忆。
B 明说 stress、pain、unhappiness，且现在有故事可讲。

questions.passage: In contrast, “beautiful art is a mode of representation which is purposive for itself, and which, although devoid of [definite] purpose, yet furthers the culture of the mental powers in reference to social communication.” Here, Kant defines an aesthetic experience as something greater than the enjoyment of mere sensation but rather the enjoyment of what he calls “reflective judgment,” which involves some gap between sensation and reality and a new mental representation and understanding of an object.
questions.prompt: What distinguishes reflective judgment from mere sensation here?
options: It excludes any mental representation of an object.
It is simply the same as passing time pleasantly.
It involves a gap between sensation and reality and a new mental understanding.
It guarantees that all viewers perceive an object identically.
questions.promptZh: 这里的反思判断与单纯感觉有什么区别？

保证所有观众理解完全一致。
analyses: A a new mental representation 明确保留表征。
B greater than...mere sensation 表示不止消遣。
C gap...new mental representation and understanding 是末尾解释。
D 没有人人一致的保证。purposive 与 devoid of definite purpose 并列是哲学限定，不擅自删括号或改成无任何意义。

evidence.quote: “reflective judgment,” which involves some gap between sensation and reality and a new mental representation and understanding of an object.

questions.passage: When Sonny Rollins, the legendary jazz saxophonist, was asked about art and, more specifically, why art matters, his reply evoked Kantian aesthetic judgments: “Technology is no savior. questions.passage: In one experiment, Berlyne manipulated two factors of geometric figures: the first was symmetry (i.e., how symmetrical and homogeneous elements were), and the other was the number of elements (i.e., one to five elements vs. numerous elements). Participants rated the simple and symmetrical figures to be the most pleasant, followed by complex and symmetrical, simple and asymmetrical, and complex and asymmetrical. Symmetry was key to pleasantness.

questions.passage: These paintings are quite shocking and grotesque, particularly in comparison to the famously serene, warm painting by Monet. After looking at each painting, participants reported how interesting or uninteresting, boring or engaging, enjoyable or unenjoyable, pleasing or displeasing, comprehensible or incomprehensible, familiar or unfamiliar each painting was. Results showed that pleasantness ratings were predicted by comprehensibleness, familiarity, and simpleness. In other words, the easier to understand and simpler the paintings were, the more pleasant they were.

questions.passage: While at the University of Virginia, I had the chance to work with two students, Erin Westgate and Nick Buttrick, with whom I read the existing literature on experimental aesthetics such as Paul Silvia’s. We wondered if reading all kinds of books early on in life helped readers appreciate more complexity and lead an intellectually rich life. So we asked over 5,000 people about their reading habits during childhood, their current cognitive styles, and their perceived levels of psychological richness.

So we asked over 5,000 people about their reading habits during childhood, their current cognitive styles, and their perceived levels of psychological richness.

questions.passage: First, as predicted, individuals who grew up reading a lot of literary fiction were indeed more attributionally complex (i.e., able to think of multiple reasons why someone might behave a certain way) and led a psychologically richer life as adults than those who did not. Second, unexpectedly, those who grew up reading a lot of romance novels were significantly less attributionally complex than those who did not. These readers seemed to “essentialize” to a greater degree than those who had read less romance.
questions.prompt: Which contrast between childhood reading groups is reported?
options: Literary-fiction readers were less attributionally complex; romance readers more so.
Compared with those who had not read much of the respective genre in childhood, heavy literary-fiction readers showed greater attributional complexity, while heavy romance readers showed less.
Both groups were reported to have exactly identical cognitive styles.
The researchers assigned adults to become lifelong romance readers.

optionsZh: 文学小说读者归因复杂性较低，言情读者较高。
分别与童年未大量阅读相应体裁者相比，大量读文学小说者归因更复杂，大量读言情者归因较少。
两组认知风格完全一样。
研究者把成人随机变成终身言情读者。
analyses: A 两个方向都反转。
B 两种比较各以未大量阅读相应体裁者为对照：文学小说关联较高，言情小说关联较低；并非直接把所有文学读者与所有言情读者逐一排序。
C 结果明确不同，不是完全一样。
D grew up reading 是既有经历，不是被分配的人生。这是群体关联，不能把阅读类型当因果或给每位读者贴能力标签。
